func replace_monster_id(current_id: String, replacement_id: String) -> bool:
	if current_id.is_empty() or replacement_id.is_empty() or not _monster_positions.has(current_id) or _monster_positions.has(replacement_id) or _character_positions.has(replacement_id):
		return false
	_monster_positions[replacement_id] = _monster_positions[current_id]
	_monster_sizes[replacement_id] = _monster_sizes[current_id]
	_monster_positions.erase(current_id)
	_monster_sizes.erase(current_id)
	return true

title: Current rolling fidelity pass — Ordinary Pool, Share, and Swap
text:
## Current rolling fidelity pass — Ordinary Pool, Share, and Swap

- The audit's two money-workflow blockers now use the declared `MONEY_ACTION` boundary. Pool, Share, and exact character/pool transfers commit synchronously inside `GameSession`; presentation emits stable character and denomination identities and never mutates wealth or calculates capacity.
- The detached Services money workspace exposes pooled, banked, and personal gold, gems, jewelry, carried load, exact Classic increments, and every core-owned unavailable reason. Pool and Share are party actions; Swap selects one character and moves five gold or one gem or jewelry per action. Done returns to exploration without another session mutation.
- Castle controls denomination order and side effects. Pool removes denomination load, Share processes jewelry then gems then gold in party order, Swap uses sounds 10051 toward a character and 663 toward the pool, Pool/Share use sound 128, and every successful operation recalculates Classic movement. Existing reward and temple wealth paths now use that same movement boundary; reward money controls also publish their source sounds.
- `FD-ECONOMY-003` records a source defect rather than silently adopting it: Castle Share can add fifteen-load jewelry to a character with only one free unit, even though Swap rejects the identical transfer. Realmz 2.0 requires the complete denomination weight to fit and leaves unassignable wealth pooled.
- Providence schema v2 needs no change. The workflow consumes mutable party wealth, package-validated character identity, race, class, conditions, and load already present in the session aggregate.
- The regenerated audit reports 3 blockers, down from 5, and 55 bidirectionally linked differential cases. Pool/Share and ordinary Swap are functional from synthetic simulation, persistence, and presentation evidence; route-open/Done audio, contextual money changing, bank semantics, and movement-time pooled-wealth handling remain explicit follow-up work.

Next application-workflow priority: ordinary AOGM battle certification or the field/camp spell blocker, selected by reachable live evidence. Banking denomination semantics and complete camp/rest remain major application-depth work, not hidden extensions of this money pass.

title: Current rolling fidelity pass — Field spells, Camp mode, and scroll cases
text:
## Current rolling fidelity pass — Field spells, Camp mode, and scroll cases

- Providence commit `202c87f1b4d856ec968760ed982f6ea6eeae3204` now preserves Castle's signed plain-character spell fields while retaining unsigned special and spell-class bytes. Negative spell costs therefore reach the runtime as fixed-power records instead of being reinterpreted as large unsigned values. The synthetic package also contains a type-13 scroll case and charged Classic item 806 parchment; schema v2 and its hash remain stable.
- Field casting validates the living caster, known slot, context, supported special, power, absolute spell-point cost, and target before mutation. One serializable character-selection continuation preserves the exact caster, spell, power, and source; duration and base damage roll once, field targets bypass combat magic resistance but retain Castle saves/protection, and committed results publish source-shaped sound and mutation facts.
- `FD-SPELL-001` corrects Castle's pre-picker spell-point loss. A cancelled or malformed target response does not spend points or consume RNG; the transaction commits only after a valid typed target response.
- Camp is now session-owned persistent mode rather than the prior invented eight-hour rest command. Entering clears location services and advances Castle's five scaled time clicks; explicit Break Camp advances two. The clock and mode survive save/restore, and movement/Search fail with exact reasons while the unresolved source continuations are unavailable.
- Every character owns five fixed typed scroll slots. While camped, a living spellcaster with an equipped type-13 case can scribe a known spell into the first empty slot by spending twice its power-scaled cost and one charge/load unit of item 806. Field scroll use spends no spell points, stages the same typed target boundary, and consumes the exact slot only after a valid response.
- `FD-SPELL-002` corrects Castle's clear-before-picker scroll behavior in both field and combat use. Invalid or cancelled targeting cannot destroy the scroll. Combat use preserves fixed power, no-SP resolution, ordinary targeting/effects, and Castle's twelve-movement/two-half-attack cost. Field-invalid discard and type-13 case transfer with its five records remain explicit gaps.
- The regenerated workflow audit reports 2 blockers and 59 bidirectionally linked differential cases. Camp/rest, item use, and field/camp casting remain partial because their named unresolved variants are not being hidden behind the completed subset.
- Godot MCP Pro opened the current synthetic package through the ordinary library, completed the five-step creator, began exploration, entered Camp, and opened the Spells workspace at 960×600. This caught and corrected two presentation defects before commit: the detached view omitted sub-hour clock minutes, and flexible scroll rows collapsed their labels into vertical text. The final frame shows `Day 1 • 00:25`, the Camped state, and full-width fixed scroll-slot rows. This is a presentation smoke test over synthetic content, not ordinary AOGM certification.

This section's original held-Rest and departure gaps are closed by the later Camp/Rest workflow pass. The former `core.party.camp` Safe Action was removed because its fixed eight-hour heal was neither the player-facing Camp command nor a source-backed reusable scenario operation.

Next application-workflow priority at this checkpoint was ordinary battle/reward acceptance; the later Camp/Rest pass closes ordinary Rest/departure while retaining timed midnight and suspicious recovery branches as explicit audit gaps.

title: Current rolling fidelity pass — Classic Camp and Rest workflow
text:
## Current rolling fidelity pass — Classic Camp and Rest workflow

- Camp remains a mode, not a fixed-duration heal. Entry clears contextual services and advances five source-scaled time clicks; explicit exit advances two. A separate typed Rest intent represents one held-control pulse, subtracting two fatigue before five time clicks so presentation repeat cadence cannot become simulation time.
- `ClockRules` now owns Classic field-time boundaries: hourly condition reduction, fatigue, character and ally spell-point recovery, and noon/midnight character and ally health recovery. Item 877 is consumed through exact inventory charge/load rules once per injured character when available.
- Land movement from camp commits fifteen time clicks before the requested move; dungeon movement commits two. Random rectangles are checked during that departure. An interrupting random battle retains a validated post-time continuation in combat state, survives save/reload and reward interactions, and resumes the requested move exactly once after battle return.
- The old Safe Scenario Action capability `core.party.camp` was removed. It performed an invented eight-hour full-heal transaction and could not truthfully represent either Castle's Camp command or held Rest loop. Scenarios may still use the explicit source-neutral time capability when authored behavior actually requests elapsed minutes.
- The focused workflow suite covers ordinary Rest, hourly recovery, noon ration use, Camp entry/exit, random choice interruption, automatic departure, active-battle save/restore, reward drain, and post-battle movement return. The audit records these as synthetic functional evidence; no ordinary AOGM Rest acceptance is claimed.
- The regenerated audit reports 60 Classic workflows, 8 host workflows, 1 blocker, 62 bidirectionally linked differential cases, and 36 functional Classic workflows. The earlier 38 count overcredited timed-event dispatch in both the clock and encounter workflows; correcting the denominator is evidence hygiene, not a product regression.

Flagged at this stage rather than copied: Castle adds its signed Poisoned condition value to half-day healing, its timed-encounter location code guards the y comparison with `recx`, and the `continueday` loop may repeat recovery around multiple records. The later timed-midnight and poisoned-boundary passes resolve these questions through complete control-flow characterization and supersede this historical uncertainty.

Next application-workflow priority: follow the regenerated audit queue. Timed midnight dispatch is now visible as its own major gap rather than being hidden inside “time complete”; ordinary AOGM Camp/Rest acceptance and the remaining scroll branches remain separate evidence tasks.

title: Current rolling fidelity pass — Guard and withdrawal reactions
text:
## Current rolling fidelity pass — Guard and withdrawal reactions

- Battle state now owns persistent Guard identities and a serializable reaction record containing mover, origin, destination, movement cost, fixed original hostile perimeter, phase, source-ordered attacker queue, cursor, and defeated-mover flag. Character movement resolves pre-move guards, every original enemy no longer adjacent with Castle's temporary plus twenty, movement for a survivor, and destination guards. Ordinary monster movement resolves party/allied guards before attacking.
- Guard and withdrawal use Castle party-slot then monster-slot order. Guard requires the flag and skips Helpless without clearing it; withdrawal does not require Guard, is suppressed only by mover Invisible, clears attacker Guard, and can let the same enemy attack once in each phase. Monster reactions use authored attack row zero. The player Guard command preserves the exact one-based 49/51 sound split and asynchronous playback; Finish Turn is now distinct and clears movement plus Guard. Implemented monster physical attacks clear their activation Guard; later ordinary missile and spell passes now do the same on successful execution.
- Age-band dialogs persist both the deferred monster attack and reaction cursor. Death-macro interruption retains the mover footprint; if CODE 119 revives it, execution resumes with the next queued attacker rather than replaying or abandoning the sequence. Impossible reaction kind/phase combinations and invalid actor/position references fail restore.
- Remake supplied adjacency and animation-queue leads, but its once-per-round `reaction_ready` economy and temporary guarding trait were rejected. Providence schema v2 already preserves every immutable combatant, condition, attack-row, and terrain fact required by this pass, so no compiler or package-contract change was needed. `.r2save` v3 remains unchanged because Guard and reaction state are additive nested combat data.
- The typed suite passes 2,193 assertions across 13 suites before aggregate closeout. Twenty-nine differential cases validate against the pinned Castle and Remake references; combat cases also validate their Providence projections where authored data is involved.

Flagged boundaries: Castle checks guards when entering movement mode before the player chooses or cancels a direction, while Realmz 2.0's typed intent already carries one legal destination. Reproducing a Guard attack on cancelled or blocked movement requires a separate begin-movement interaction and is not inferred here. Retreating-monster withdrawal, possessed-character auto-guard, target-everybody Guard omission, friendly swaps, and spell-field collision remain unresolved. `getup.c` also appears to index `monster[q[up]]` with initiative IDs that start at ten; this unsafe status-display access is not reproduced.

title: Source/control-flow evidence
text:
## Source/control-flow evidence

At Castle commit `491816ad60037394f92c428e99c004494d3c28b3`, `src/realmz_orig/share-movecost-dialog.c:44` implements `Rand(range)` by calling QuickDraw `Random()`, taking the absolute signed result, and returning `1 + (raw * range) / 32768`. Positive ranges produce Realmz's inclusive 1…range scaling. The signed-short parameter also permits zero and negative authored/effective ranges; those still consume a draw and use C integer truncation toward zero.

The same commit's `src/MemoryManager.cpp:286` documents the original signed range but deliberately supplies host random bytes in the SDL port. Castle therefore remains evidence for scaling and draw order, not for a deterministic historical seed sequence.

title: Macintosh algorithm evidence
text:
## Macintosh algorithm evidence

Apple's *develop* Issue 21 states that QuickDraw updates the unsigned 32-bit `randSeed` with `randSeed = (randSeed * 16807) mod 2147483647` and returns a signed 16-bit number. [Archived issue text](https://preserve.mactech.com/articles/develop/issue_21/21macqaa.html)

*Inside Macintosh: Operating System Utilities* specifies that `Random` is determined solely by `randSeed`, initializes from seed 1, and returns uniformly from -32767 through 32767. [Archived Apple reference](https://dev.os9.ca/techpubs/mac/OSUtilities/OSUtilities-63.html)

The recovered QuickDraw routine returns the signed low word of the updated seed and maps low word `0x8000` to zero, preserving the documented exclusion of -32768. Runtime-unit vectors starting with seed 1 observe seed states `16807`, `282475249`, and `1622650073`; the corresponding signed raw values begin `16807`, `15089`, and `-21287`. Castle scaling at range 100 yields 52, 47, and 65.

title: Runtime contract
text:
## Runtime contract

- The host supplies one seed; normalization maps zero to QuickDraw's default seed 1.
- State and draw count are session-owned and saved.
- Every trace entry records draw index, semantic tag, range, raw value, and result.
- `ScriptedRng` accepts signed raw values for branch-equivalent source/oracle fixtures.
- `draw_classic` preserves Castle's signed-short range formula for source paths where zero or negative effective values are legal; the ordinary `draw` API continues to reject invalid positive-die ranges.
- No core code may call Godot randomness or derive a seed from wall-clock time.

Evidence labels: the Castle function and Macintosh references are `source-control-flow`; the seed/scaling vectors are `runtime-unit`. A separate `castle-runtime` fixture is still required before claiming an original Mac executable sequence observation.

title: Delivery roadmap
text:
# Delivery roadmap

Status values describe current evidence, not intent. A phase completes only when its exit gate is proven.

- **Architecture complete** means the approved ownership and boundary contracts exist and pass their architecture gates.
- **Route-certified** means one bounded scripted route completed through the normal runtime; it does not prove optional branches or the surrounding application.
- **Functionally complete** means every required axis and variant for a workflow passes the generated application audit.
- **Live-certified** means a functionally complete workflow also has accepted presentation and the required ordinary-play or cross-platform evidence.

title: Current phase — Audit-guided parity convergence
text:
## Current phase — Audit-guided parity convergence

The completed application audit remains the fixed denominator, and the rolling differential ledger remains the authority for disputed behavior. Delivery now emphasizes convergence: each 3–5-workflow batch includes ordinary-play certification, prioritizes missing and partial workflows over deeper edge cases in functional workflows, and reports functional/certified count deltas from an explicit baseline. The 60/25/15 planning allocation and archaeology stop rule are defined in `docs/development.md` and enforced structurally by the workflow-inventory validator.

The completed **Ordinary AOGM combat certification** batch exercised representative physical attack, combat spell, explicit character retreat, ordinary rewards, an actual level result, spell selection, save/restore, and terminal return through the ordinary UI. The completed **Final ordinary AOGM service lifecycle certification** batch then exercised an exact charged-item Trade, every visible Temple service with a real successful mutation and Castle's paid no-effect behavior, and the full Shop lifecycle: buy, paid identification, sale to normalized buyback stock, save/reload while the Shop request remained pending, buyback purchase, and Leave to exploration. All three workflows now carry ordinary AOGM evidence.

Shop and Temple are no longer standing implementation priorities. The only retained Shop gap is low-priority Providence parity for native empty-slot ordering; it does not block the normalized buyback workflow or AOGM play. Future service work requires an observed campaign defect or content that demonstrably depends on that native ordering. The next batch is selected from the regenerated non-service audit queue rather than extending Shop or Temple edge cases.

Current combat-interface convergence restores Castle's far-click one-step direction projection, detached shown-target facts, Reveal Friends, camera Center/Next/Previous, source-ordered physical attack feedback, Auto, Delay, Bandage, Turn Undead, bounded movement-only Undo, fixed-power combat scroll use through battlefield-native targeting, and character-owned Fast Spell bindings/shortcuts through ordinary typed casting. Realmz Rebuilt now owns the complete pinned 142-resource integrated sound bank; Providence commit `8fead345c0d13b74fe08b26060ab538073a77df3` packages only scenario-owned exact sound overrides. A clean AOGM export and live MCP session prove application fallback for integrated sound 147, scenario ownership for sound 24000, and a non-overlapping 960x600 setup shell. Human auditory comparison and ordinary combat-layout acceptance remain batch closeout evidence; Auto Weapon Switch policy and Undo's runtime-unobserved cursor edges remain current work.

Missing Fast Spell and Allies/Bestiary remain leading non-service implementation candidates unless the regenerated audit identifies a more reachable AOGM application gap. Historical rolling-pass entries below remain evidence of completed slices, not standing instructions to continue their old “next priority” notes.

title: Current rolling fidelity pass — Charged spell-item use
text:
## Current rolling fidelity pass — Charged spell-item use

- Castle `items`, `canuse`, `getchoice`, and combat choice establish the bounded common path: an item's second special field names a spell, `abs(sp1)` supplies fixed power, positive charges lose one charge and per-charge load, negative authored charges remain reusable, and the item sound is requested at its ID plus 600. Field type 5 targets the user, target types above 2 target the party, and other field forms stage a character choice; combat returns through the ordinary spell-target lifecycle. Item use spends no spell points or known-spell slot.
- `GameSession` now owns field item selection through a typed, saveable continuation. It rolls field power value 8 through the central RNG before staging the target, rejects stale/duplicate/wrong-count responses without spending a charge, and publishes exact item, spell, target, power, charge, load, and sound facts only after commit.
- `CombatFlow` exposes only source-probed fixed-power actor and automatic-group item uses for the active character. The scenario runtime and direct session both carry exact item-instance and target IDs; malformed responses are transactional. A committed use spends Castle's twelve movement and two half-attack units, does not spend spell points or count as a memorized-spell cast, and returns through the ordinary battle interaction.
- Inventory and battle presentation consume detached availability/options and emit stable identities only. The fixture gallery includes a populated charged-item combat state; no presenter derives permission, targets, power, charges, range, or spell effects.
- Providence schema v2 already emits item type, category/restriction fields, charges, per-charge weight, drop flag, sound, all five special fields, and referenced spell records. No compiler, package-schema, or save-envelope revision was required.
- The audit now reports 5 blockers, down from 6, with 53 bidirectionally linked differential cases. `classic.inventory.use-item` remains partial because distinct item families are not being hidden behind the implemented subset.
- The complete typed suite passes 2,999 assertions across 15 suites, including direct-session and scenario-host combat item requests, invalid-response transactionality, random-power rollback/staging, target-selection restoration, fixed-power continuation integrity, and unidentified-name safety.

Flagged rather than copied: Castle decrements a positive charge before the abortable field picker and ignores `getchoice`'s return value, which appears to lose a charge on cancellation. A controlled Castle fixture must settle that observable before a named preservation/correction decision. Door/XAP items, item type 13 scrolls, missile-class items, random-power combat staging, battlefield area/repeated targets, and broader spell specials remain explicit unavailable families.

Next application-workflow priority: take the highest remaining AOGM blocker from the regenerated audit—field/camp spells and scrolls, manual Pool/Share/Swap access, or complete camp/rest—after checking its Providence prerequisites and ordinary AOGM reachability. Schedule a live charged-item observation alongside the next stable AOGM route rather than upgrading synthetic evidence to certification.

title: Current rolling fidelity pass — Ordinary rewards and terminal battle return
text:
## Current rolling fidelity pass — Ordinary rewards and terminal battle return

- Scenario treasures and ordinary battle rewards now enter one typed, session-owned reward continuation. Wealth, shared experience, and exact pending `ItemInstance` values commit once; assignment, leave-behind, capacity failure, Pool, Share, denomination Swap, Detect Magic, Identify Objects, completion confirmation, and every pending request survive canonical save/restore.
- Dead or animated recipients are excluded from experience in source order. Each positive recipient gains at most one level during one reward close, matching Castle's caller control flow rather than automatically consuming every positive threshold. The source-backed level transaction publishes a dedicated result stage; eligible spellcasters then receive a serializable spell-selection stage that permits valid unspent points.
- Ordinary victory now proceeds through ally selection, exact fumble recovery, prevalidated monster rewards, treasure, level results, spell selection, after-message, cleanup, and one return to the originating VM or exploration continuation. Defeat and full-party retreat complete without reward draws; a character who escapes before the remaining party wins is excluded from that victory's experience division. Re-entry cannot reroll or replay a completed reward.
- `FD-ECONOMY-002` permits exact-instance treasure assignment at precisely maximum load. Castle's strict-less-than test rejects that legal boundary and separately ignores charge weight; the chosen rule uses one complete instance weight for both validation and mutation.
- The presentation gallery covers populated, empty, capacity-blocked, unidentified, oversized, level-result, and spell-selection states. This is synthetic functional evidence, not ordinary AOGM acceptance.
- The workflow audit now derives 6 blockers, down from 9, and the differential ledger validates 52 bidirectionally linked cases.
- The complete typed suite passes 2,947 assertions across 15 suites, including terminal cleanup through both direct-session and VM-owned battle continuations.

Flagged rather than copied: Castle's two less-than-ten parchment/ration drops, battle mode 5 XP-only behavior, battle mode 10 restoration behavior, opcode 48 bonus treasure, and progression beyond the thirtieth threshold still require controlled fixtures or package-contract evidence. The complete ordinary AOGM battle/reward/return presentation also remains uncertified.

Scenario-owned ordinary total defeat now crosses a typed, saveable VM-to-session handoff into Global Party Death. Unrecovered defeat closes without running later scenario instructions; opcode 119 revival suppresses rewards, releases combat once, and resumes the exact Classic or Safe caller. Castle's mode-10 encounter restart and opcode-56 target-minus-one backup/experience-loss return remain explicit unavailable branches. Providence schema v2 already retains the positional EDCD words needed for these callers, so the remaining work is runtime behavior and controlled oracle adjudication rather than a presumed schema revision.

Next application-workflow priority: use the regenerated audit queue for remaining AOGM blockers—ordinary item use/targeting, field and camp spells or scrolls, full Pool/Share/Swap access, bank denomination behavior, and complete camp/rest—while scheduling one ordinary AOGM battle acceptance pass as soon as a stable reachable battle is available.

title: Current rolling fidelity pass — Classic temple and contextual services
text:

The no-bank pooled-wealth departure gap recorded during this temple pass is now closed by the later typed Swap continuation. The application workflow audit selected ordinary treasure and terminal battle return as the next complete tranche. The implementation below closes the default reward path while retaining Castle's special battle modes and incidental random drops as explicit evidence gaps.

title: Current rolling fidelity pass — Ordinary shop and paid identification
text:
## Current rolling fidelity pass — Ordinary shop and paid identification

- Remake supplied the application-workflow lead: a dedicated stock/party workspace, buyback handling, equipment guards, and paid-identification controls. Castle, not Remake's generic rate model, determined the rules.

title: FD-ECONOMY-003 — Require complete denomination capacity during Share
text:
## FD-ECONOMY-003 — Require complete denomination capacity during Share

- Affected rule: Classic Share when pooled jewelry is assigned to a character with fewer than fifteen load units free.
- Castle evidence: commit `491816ad60037394f92c428e99c004494d3c28b3`, `src/realmz_orig/share-movecost-dialog.c`, `share`, lines 5–40, and `src/realmz_orig/swap.c`, `swap`, lines 129–159. Share tests only `current load < maximum load` before adding fifteen for jewelry; Swap tests the complete added weight before the same transfer.
- Observable source inconsistency: a character at load 99 of 100 receives one jewelry through Share and becomes load 114, while the adjacent manual Swap path rejects that transfer. The synthetic source-observation fixture is `tests/fixtures/oracle/money-share-capacity-correction.json`, SHA-256 `b5cd34bb12db32b2b2213ecac35df289ee696b18b5f44758478b0a1c49559aeb`. This is `source-control-flow` evidence, not a Castle-runtime claim.
- Player-facing problem: the one-click distribution command can create an overloaded character that the manual money command correctly identifies as unable to carry the same denomination.
- Chosen 2.0 behavior: Share retains Castle's jewelry, gems, then gold order and one-unit-per-character passes, but assigns a denomination only when its complete weight fits at or below maximum load. Unassignable wealth remains in the pool with a typed reason.
- Tests: `test_money_workflow.gd` records the Castle source result, verifies the corrected capacity result, covers all three denominations, source order, sounds, movement recalculation, typed intents, and save restoration. `test_classic_ui_system.gd` verifies detached disabled reasons. The differential case is `economy.pool-share`.
- Legacy quirk: none. Overloading through Share contradicts Swap and the ordinary maximum-load invariant.

title: FD-INVENTORY-001 — Safe equipped-item trade
text:
## FD-INVENTORY-001 — Safe equipped-item trade

- Affected rule: moving an equipped carried item between party members in the ordinary two-character Trade workspace.
- Castle evidence: commit `491816ad60037394f92c428e99c004494d3c28b3`, `src/realmz_orig/items.c`, `items`, lines 950–979; `moveicon.c`, `moveicon`, lines 221–259, 353–440, and 615–655; and `removeitem.c`, `removeitem`, lines 5–102. Trade copies an equipped item to the recipient with its equipped flag cleared, but deletes the source record directly instead of invoking `removeitem`. The `canuse` failure changes cursor/sound without preventing the move.
- Observable source inconsistency: an equipped curse can bypass the ordinary curse-removal lock, and stored source-character equipment bonuses are not explicitly reversed even though the item record is gone. The synthetic source-observation fixture is `tests/fixtures/oracle/equipped-item-trade-correction.json`, SHA-256 `465fb2d73ae1d585a932a95a9ff0562719b3bfe90159c20eef85444f7bbf4d76`. This is `source-control-flow` evidence, not a Castle-runtime claim.
- Player-facing problem: Trade can remove a supposedly locked curse and leave the source character benefiting from equipment no longer carried. Those outcomes contradict the ordinary Equip/Unequip workflow and create state that cannot be derived from current inventory.
- Chosen 2.0 behavior: allow an equipped ordinary item to transfer and force the recipient instance unequipped, matching Castle's record outcome. Derived values always follow the current equipped instances. Reject trading an equipped cursed item, so the curse cannot bypass its source-backed removal lock.
- Tests: `test_inventory_session.gd` verifies equipped ordinary transfer, recipient unequipped state, exact load movement, and equipped-curse rejection. The differential case is `inventory.carried-item-workflow`.
- Legacy quirk: none. Stale derived bonuses and removable equipped curses are contradictory state, not useful authored behavior.

title: FD-CHARACTER-002 — Human appearance-set zero alias
text:
## FD-CHARACTER-002 — Human appearance-set zero alias

- Affected rule: the initial and recommended portrait/tactical icon for a Human character whose Data Race `defaulticonset` is zero.
- Castle evidence: commit `491816ad60037394f92c428e99c004494d3c28b3`, `src/realmz_orig/newcharacter.c`, `CharacterGen`; `src/realmz_orig/portrait-picklock.c`, `portrait`; `src/realmz_orig/iconpict.c`, `iconpicture`; and `src/realmz_orig/main.c`, the Portraits/Tacticals resource-fork opens. Initial creation computes portrait `251 + defaulticonset*6` and tactical `9000 - 257 + portrait`; the portrait picker applies the same zero-set offset. The browseable forks instead contain portraits 257–376 and tacticals 9000–9119. The imported Human record stores set zero, and decoded portrait 257 matches the first named Human portrait used by the functional Remake reference.
- Observable source inconsistency: the literal Human initial values are 251 and 8994, neither of which belongs to the browseable character catalogs, while the picker/catalog pairing begins at 257/9000. This conclusion combines complete pinned source flow with direct resource inventory; it is not presented as a Castle-runtime capture.
- Player-facing problem: preserving the literal formula would create a Human with unavailable art and would place no actual Human portraits in the recommended group.
- Chosen 2.0 behavior: treat stored set zero as an alias of the first browseable six-portrait set. A default Human receives portrait 257 and tactical icon 9000; explicit selection uses the corresponding offset. Set one remains a valid alias for the same first portrait set, and all positive set values otherwise retain Castle's formula.
- Tests: Providence validates the zero/set-one alias and emits exactly 120 role-labelled portraits plus 120 tactical icons. Package, session, UI, save/restore, and vault tests verify complete catalogs, stable IDs, role rejection, Human defaults, and immutable revision eligibility. The differential case is `character.appearance-catalog-and-human-default`.
- Legacy quirk: none. Missing resources are not useful authored behavior, and no compatibility profile is introduced.

text:

title: FD-CHARACTER-001 — Bounded trained-ability records
text:
## FD-CHARACTER-001 — Bounded trained-ability records

- Affected rule: initialization and level-up of the character's fifteen-slot trained-ability array.
- Castle evidence: commit `491816ad60037394f92c428e99c004494d3c28b3`, `src/realmz_orig/updatespec.c`, `updatespec`, lines 49–97, and `src/realmz_orig/structs.h`, lines 60, 94, and 314. `character.spec` has fifteen slots, but both race and caste `specialability` records have only fourteen. The initialization and level-up loops nevertheless run through slot fourteen, reading beyond both authored arrays; the neighboring twelve-slot `character.special` array is a separate racial combat-modifier field.
- Observable oracle behavior, determined from the complete source flow: the fifteenth iteration aliases adjacent struct storage and can conditionally add or roll a value that is not an authored trained ability. Its value and RNG effect depend on unrelated record fields rather than a defined file-format slot. The synthetic source-observation fixture is `tests/fixtures/oracle/character-ability-index-boundary-correction.json`, SHA-256 `31715ad5796826ed192f2eb8ecad905dc6ea07ad0d068dcbdc2cb35d9b6f118c`. This is `source-control-flow` evidence, not a Castle-runtime claim.
- Player-facing problem: changing an unrelated race/caste field can alter a hidden ability or consume an extra gameplay draw during character creation and every level-up. Conflating `special` with `spec` would also make racial combat modifiers double as thief/application skills.
- Chosen 2.0 behavior: preserve fifteen trained-ability slots in character/save state, import and evaluate only the fourteen authored race/caste values, and hold slot fourteen at zero without a draw. Keep the twelve racial combat modifiers in their independent `specials` field. Strength/Dexterity modifiers and clamps retain Castle's authored fourteen-slot behavior.
- Tests: `_test_character_creation_and_leveling` verifies exact level-three values, draw count, the zero unauthored slot, the separate racial modifiers, victory threshold, condition threshold, and two-hand statistic. Package tests reject ability arrays of the wrong length. The differential case is `character.trained-ability-index-boundary`.
- Legacy quirk: none. Adjacent-struct reads are not authored scenario data and cannot be represented portably.

title: `.realmz2`
text:
## `.realmz2`

A deterministic ZIP contains canonical minified JSON and content-addressed media:

- `manifest.json`: format/version, campaign/content IDs, compiler provenance, engine requirements, start location, capability inventory, file hashes, package hash.
- `content.json`: Realmz definitions and text.
- `world.json`: maps, authoritative topology, APs/XAPs, transitions, random rectangles, timed encounters, and immutable metadata.
- `scenario.json`: Classic instructions, Scenario Action programs, state definitions, and migrations.
- `assets/index.json` plus hashed media payloads.

Providence owns the schema. The runtime mirror under `contracts` is byte-identical and independently enforced. The package excludes editor layout, absolute paths, native raw bytes, compatibility annexes, and archaeology artifacts.

Schema v2 replaces the unpublished v1 contract. The mirrored schema is SHA-256 `8167835e4db54d97eb90a263967d472f8108dbf63c3bc0ebd5d723441bdadbaf` from Providence commit `899a191272643295d0c7d0c00d23a073407870fa`. It retains the v1 world, scenario, media, and direct Realmz definition contracts while adding typed campaign display metadata (`name`, `version`, `author`, `contact`, `description`, and `splashAssetId`), Data SC aggregate recommended/maximum party levels and an explicit source-authorship flag, party/level restrictions, typed alternate Monster Sets, exactly thirty one-based race/caste profiles with aligned eligibility, each race's exact five-by-fifteen signed aging table and fourteen authored ability bonuses, both fourteen-value caste ability rows, all thirty caste victory thresholds, distinct bounded monster `requiredWeapon` and `magicToHit` fields, complete Classic battle-terrain catalogs, signed spell-record fields such as negative fixed power/cost, and exact nullable Start Game, Party Death, End Adventure, Shop, and Temple application-hook program references. Battle `distance` remains a separate initial-placement input. Providence's canonical project and native compatibility annex remain outside the package. Canonical schema bytes use LF line endings so the compiler and runtime hash the same contract on Windows.

The schema-v2 world contract uses normalized directional edges and explicit features; Castle's packed dungeon fields and Providence's Layout record remain compiler inputs, not runtime map models. Each cell names a base tileset/tile and a nullable image-overlay asset. Placed AP references compile in native record order and retain `classicRecordIndex`; duplicate record identities on one map fail runtime validation. Placed AP headers compile to a typed `postActionLocation`; XAPs use `null`, and tile mutation remains an explicit scenario instruction. Random rectangles retain signed 1-in-10,000 chances, battle ranges, three random-door slots, only/option behavior, and media IDs. Its content contract carries direct Simple/Complex/Thief/Timed Encounter records, a distinct Classic option-label table, and direct race, caste, item, spell, monster, battle, treasure, and shop definitions. The base monster catalog represents Normal Monsters; optional typed sets `-1` and `1` contain complete reachable replacements from Data MD-1 and Data MD1 with unique stable identities. A package may not emit a partial set or ambiguous replacement. Providence merges 799 nonzero bundled Classic item identities with scenario supplies/overrides and compiles standard Data S records to packed class/level/slot identities; custom Data Spell slot 0 is packed ID 5101 and slot 104 is 5715. Monster weapon restrictions retain the signed Data MD byte as `requiredWeapon`; `magicToHit` is its independent weapon-plus threshold. Battle records retain their unrelated placement `distance`, explicit monster slots, coordinates, and traitor inversion. Its scenario contract contains trigger/program references, exact application-hook program IDs, preserved `ClassicAction` instructions, typed `CallScenarioAction` instructions, compiled Safe bytecode, versioned action-state definitions, and migrations. It does not contain Safe visual/source AST, behavior anchors, authoring modes, or sandbox source.

For every package with a reachable battle, `world.json` now carries immutable `battleTerrainSets` and each map identifies its effective set. A land set contains its active landlook records 0 through 200 followed by shared `Combat Data BD` records 201 through 400; the active landlook therefore wins Castle's overlapping tile 200 exactly once. The dungeon set contains shared records 200 through 400. Every tile retains signed sound, time, solid, boat, and forest values, exact boolean flags, and the 3×3 `combatBuild`; incomplete ranges or malformed builds fail both export and runtime construction. These are immutable construction inputs, not an alternate exploration topology. Tactical positions, battlefield generation, proximity-gated melee, and Guard/withdrawal reactions use session-owned combat geometry and serialized cursors. Ranged attacks remain disabled until projectile range, costs, and resolution are source-owned.

Managed Providence media and decoded imported scenario resource-catalog pictures/icons/sounds become content-addressed package payloads. Classic resource identity is the exact four-character type plus signed ID; case and trailing spaces are significant, and equal numbers in `PICT`, `cicn`, and `snd ` are unrelated resources. Scenario-managed media replaces the imported scenario-catalog entry for the same key. Realmz's integrated `snd ` bank is versioned application media and is not copied into every campaign; a packaged exact sound key is an explicit scenario override and resolves before the application fallback. Package ambiguity never falls through to a plausible built-in resource. Missing integrated media is a Realmz Rebuilt build/install defect, not a campaign-readiness defect. This deterministic composition preserves Castle's normal scenario-before-application result without exposing its mutable global resource-file cursor. Providence and the runtime independently reject duplicate package asset IDs and exact package resource keys. Application PICT/CICN migration remains resource-family-specific because current map, appearance, and battle contracts still carry package asset IDs. Every referenced map tileset is a required content-addressed PNG with explicit grid metadata; Providence normalizes Classic PICT 302's fixed dungeon-composition region to a 4×4 runtime atlas and, for reachable battles, emits the complete 20×20 image as the exact `classic-battle-tiles-302` battle atlas. Castle's effective combat graphics combine the active landlook for battle tile IDs 1–200 with that shared atlas for IDs 201–400. Classic negative land values compile as the landlook's base terrain plus a content-addressed `cicn` overlay rather than masquerading as a tileset index. Absolute paths and resource-fork bytes never enter the package.

Every package also carries the complete selectable Classic character appearance catalogs: portrait `cicn` 257–376 and tactical `cicn` 9000–9119. Each effective entry has an explicit `portrait` or `combat-icon` role, stable asset identity, decoded PNG dimensions, and ordinary exact-key precedence. Providence and the runtime both reject a missing, duplicate, wrongly typed, or undecodable entry. Castle's Human Data Race value stores portrait set zero even though the browseable Portraits fork starts at 257; `FD-CHARACTER-002` deliberately aliases set zero to the first real six-image set rather than requesting unavailable `cicn` 251–256.

`PackageRepository` rejects unsafe/extra entries, noncanonical entry order, schema or capability drift, per-file size/hash mismatches, package-hash mismatches, malformed topology, duplicate identities, incomplete character appearance catalogs, unresolved map/trigger/program/action references, unsupported Classic opcodes, invalid Scenario Action namespaces or callers, argument/type mismatches, over...

title: `.r2char`
text:
## `.r2char`

Reusable character revisions are separate from `.r2save`. A record contains a stable character ID, immutable revision hash, rules version, source campaign/package provenance, publication metadata, complete detached character state, inventory/spells, and source revision. `CharacterVaultRepository` stores revisions under `user://characters/<character-id>/`, validates the requested character and revision identities on every read, retains one recoverable backup, and archives instead of deleting. The host exposes current and earlier immutable revisions, exact target-campaign eligibility, archive confirmation, and recovery without allowing presentation to touch files. Import is a typed session intent; eligibility failures identify missing definitions, restrictions, level limits, incompatible race/class relationships, or unavailable/wrong-role portrait and combat-icon IDs. The session recomputes personal carried load from the target package's immutable item weights and the imported wealth rather than trusting a stale revision total; an over-limit result is ineligible without stripping or substituting content. Finalizing a newly created character yields a typed, saveable publication confirmation. Acceptance publishes only after the session has committed the character and cleared the interaction; decline has no repository side effect. Ordinary campaign changes never write back implicitly.

`SaveRepository` writes envelope v3 by creating a temporary file, parsing it back into typed state, rotating one backup, and renaming the verified temporary file into the slot. Ordered pure migrations take v1 through v2's session-interaction/random-region fields and then add v3's `actionPointDestinationDepth` to nonempty post-move continuations. V3 also validates the alternate direct combat-death-macro, carried-item drop, post-battle ally-selection, and fumble-recovery continuation shapes against their matching state and pending request. `GameSession.snapshot()` returns a detached aggregate, including all gameplay-domain state, VM frames, pending request/continuation, Scenario Action state, and host continuation. Restore constructs and validates replacement state, RNG, VM, action-state, session-interaction, continuation, item identities, and each character's package-derived carried-load total before replacing the active session; any mismatch leaves the current session untouched.

title: Browser search
text:
## Browser search

Search accepts normal words, quoted phrases, and filters:

- `kind:function` — entity kind such as `module`, `file`, `class`, `function`, `test`, `concept`, `doc-section`, or `dox`.
- `path:src/scenario` — path prefix.
- `module:scenario-vm` — overview/module identifier.
- `dox:src/core` — governing DOX scope.
- `test:scenario` — related test text.
- `flow:save` — related flow text.
- `unknown:true` — unresolved relationships and diagnostics.

Select a result to see source lines, callers, dependencies, tests, documents, DOX constraints, flows, and evidence. Source links use the embedded snapshot and remain usable when the HTML is opened with `file://`.

Selecting a source reference updates the URL hash with the stable entity, path, and line. Those links work with browser back/forward navigation and include a copyable `path:line` reference. Graph node selections stay pinned after the pointer is released; click the graph background to clear them. The inspector favors readable source/context space, while search results stay compact and scroll within a bounded panel. The graph supports node selection, upstream/downstream highlighting, complete flow highlighting, zoom, fit, and drag repositioning.

title: Current rolling fidelity pass — Per-character Escape and routed monsters
text:
## Current rolling fidelity pass — Per-character Escape and routed monsters

- Explicit Escape is now a source-backed per-character operation. It uses Castle's integer-truncated Euclidean nearest-enemy range, permits exactly ten, rejects Helpless, traitor, Confused, Tangled, and Slow actors, asks `Embrace Cowardice` versus `Stay and Fight`, removes only the accepting character, and adds exactly 200 prestige penalty. Battle continues while another living loyal character remains on the field; escaped living characters receive no battle experience.
- Battlefield-edge movement is a distinct Escape route. Entering the outer band prompts before ordinary terrain collision, while a character already in the outermost band is forced out. The detached combat view and typed battle interaction mark edge options explicitly instead of presenting them as ordinary movement.
- `CombatState` now persists sorted `retreatedCharacterIds`. Restore therefore accepts a deliberately escaped living character without weakening corruption checks for an arbitrarily missing living actor. Direct and scenario-hosted Escape confirmations use the existing typed `yes_no` shape and survive `.r2save` v3 or VM restoration without replay.
- RUNS_AWAY monsters move away from their retained target through the existing bounded topology probe, snapshot source-ordered adjacent enemies, receive withdrawal attacks before each committed step, and leave when the destination reaches Castle's edge band. Hostile flight sets zero stamina-equivalent health, removes the footprint, grants ordinary defeated-monster rewards, and does not request a death macro.
- Remake supplied the per-character `fled_battle` and edge-removal leads, but its `distance_to <= 10` rejects Castle's legal exact-ten case, omits condition/confirmation gates, and its routed AI flees from an enemy barycenter. Those differences were rejected in favor of Castle's retained-target flow. Providence schema v2 already carries all required immutable monster and terrain facts, so no compiler/package change was needed.
- Flagged rather than guessed: Castle can read `pos[-1]` when a routed monster has no retained target; 2.0 reports `retreat-target-unresolved`. Its mandatory-ally branch commits the edge step before flipping deltas that are recomputed on the next loop; 2.0 stops there and reports `mandatory-ally-edge-retreat-unresolved`. These are not claimed as corrected Classic behavior without runtime evidence and a named decision.

title: Current follow-on tranche — Classic-wide application system (in progress)
text:

title: Current rolling fidelity pass — Ordinary physical projectiles
text:

The runtime mirror independently requires six entries, permits empty strings, rejects unresolved nonempty item IDs, and the synthetic fixture proves an empty slot one cannot collapse.

Keep random-power and nonphysical projectiles, possessed-character cadence, permanent-Tangle movement, Castle haste/display contradictions, random-weapon-table spawn-origin split, pre-direction movement cancellation, and the top-tile path typo separate until each has its own evidence.

title: Current rolling fidelity pass — Spell death-macro queue
text:
## Current rolling fidelity pass — Spell death-macro queue

- Castle does not dispatch each spell-killed monster's death macro immediately. `resolvespell` reaches `killbody` while `inspell` is active, `killbody` appends the macro and subject to `todoque`, and `emptyque` drains that queue before battle outcome or actor progression. Remake supplied a useful FIFO implementation lead, but Castle establishes the spell-scoped timing and authored subject identity.
- `CombatState` now owns and serializes the ordered spell death-macro IDs, original caster, and whether the caster should advance when the queue drains. The core validates the exact completed subject, removes only that still-dead subject, requests the next macro in source order, and defers victory or caster advancement until no queued macro remains.
- Both direct-session and scenario-owned death-macro continuations preserve the queue through typed interaction and `.r2save` v3 restoration. Older continuation data defaults to the prior immediate-macro allegiance behavior, while new queued entries carry an explicit host policy.
- Cross-function review prevented an overcorrection: the queued `killbody` path itself does not reset monster allegiance, but Classic opcode 119 explicitly does. The host no longer resets allegiance unconditionally; an authored revival still does so through the opcode implementation.
- Multiple-entry tests prove exact FIFO order, stale-cursor rejection, per-subject occupancy removal, and retained original caster state. A yielding macro test proves whole-session restoration and that a macro without an allegiance-changing opcode leaves the source allegiance intact.
- The typed suite passes 2,290 assertions across 13 suites. Group spell casting remains explicit because Castle rolls shared duration/base damage and charges once before iterating targets; invoking the single-target resolver repeatedly would alter both RNG and cost.

Next rolling priority: implement source-ordered automatic all-friendly/all-enemy/everybody damage resolution over one shared cast transaction. First resolve Providence's apparent target-type inventory gap for Castle value 12 and adjudicate the target-everybody Guard omission; do not silently normalize either behavior.

title: Current rolling fidelity pass — Player automatic group spells
text:
## Current rolling fidelity pass — Player automatic group spells

- Player target types 9, 10, and 12 now use one automatic cast option and select living positioned participants in Castle party-slot then monster-slot order. The UI labels the group without fabricating a target combatant or meaningless HP total.
- `MagicRules` spends once and rolls one duration/base-damage value before applying resistance, save, elemental protection, and damage independently to each typed target. `CombatFlow` spends two half-attacks and twelve movement once and queues defeated monsters' macros in the resulting source order.

Realmz 2.0 reports `monster-group-spell-power-resource-anomaly` until a controlled Castle fixture or named correction determines intended behavior.

title: Current rolling fidelity pass — Player spatial area spells
text:
## Current rolling fidelity pass — Player spatial area spells

- Castle establishes that target types 3 and 4 are one-center spatial transactions, but target type 0 is not. Type 3 uses the spell's fixed Data AD shape; type 4 uses cast power. Type 0 performs multiple independent target selections and reruns `spelltargets` plus `resolvespell` for each selection, including fresh duration/base-damage rolls, so it remains explicitly unavailable rather than being folded into the area path.

A separate named fidelity correction is not asserted because the out-of-bounds Castle result is not a stable gameplay behavior.

Reflection can consume targeting-stage draws and redirect to the caster; rotation selects adjacent Data AD records rather than applying a geometric transform; queued fields create persistent collision state before resolution. Player and monster queued-field spells now fail explicitly rather than dealing immediate damage while silently omitting that state.

- The typed suite passes 2,332 assertions across 13 suites. Thirty-six differential cases target the pinned Castle, Remake, and Providence checkpoints.

Next rolling priority: implement the target-type 0 repeated-selection continuation or take a narrower active-content spell branch after inventorying certified campaign use. title: Current rolling fidelity pass — Repeated actor-target spells
text:

Ordinary reflection is now owned by the following pass.

title: Current rolling fidelity pass — Ordinary spell reflection and opposed-monster targets
text:
## Current rolling fidelity pass — Ordinary spell reflection and opposed-monster targets

- Castle's ordinary target types zero and one check Reflecting Spells once on the originally selected party or monster actor. Results one through thirty-three replace that actor with active caster `q[up]` before duration, damage, the original monster's above-100 exclusion, resistance, saves, or protection. The redirected caster is resolved once; its own reflection condition does not recurse.
- `SpellTargetSelection` and `GroupSpellResolution` now retain original and effective actor identity plus a typed reflection flag. Player single and repeated casts use that contract, and a reflecting actor remains visible in the repeated-target picker instead of being silently suppressed.
- Monster casting now samples the complete native space: party slots, slot nine's gap, and monster slots ten onward. Opposed monsters resolve through the same source-ordered monster resistance/save/protection path, while reflected monster casts can strike the caster. Castle queues a reflected caster's death during `inspell`, finishes its remaining authored magic attacks without another stamina check, and drains the macros afterward. Repeated post-death hits append duplicate records to Castle's fixed 100-entry queue; 2.0 now preserves that bounded order, keeps occupancy until the subject's final record, and serializes the complete caster continuation.
- The implementation deliberately does not spread this rule to every spell shape. Castle's automatic groups bypass ordinary reflection; area footprints can test one large actor repeatedly; intelligent area scoring consumes reflection RNG before the actual cast; queued fields explicitly suppress reflection. Those suspicious or distinct branches remain unavailable until separately adjudicated.
- Providence requires no new package change for reflection: schema v2 already preserves target type, ordinary spell fields, and all forty signed monster conditions at the current compiler checkpoint. The knowledge-graph format-enrichment lock targets Realmz commit `4089d550ab606172bac850ac055677c36c6ff547`, not the pinned Castle oracle, so this pass uses direct source/control-flow evidence rather than applying graph conclusions across revisions.
- The focused typed suite passes 2,388 assertions across 13 suites before aggregate closeout. Thirty-nine differential cases now distinguish ordinary reflection from area/group/field behavior.

Flagged boundaries: friendly monster targeting under `cannot == 4`, nonzero-size open-space/summoning placement, rotatable masks, queued fields, item/fast/random-power casting, class-nine nonphysical effects, monster group anomalies, and target type 11 remain separate.

title: Current rolling fidelity pass — Native race/caste identity and ordinary startup
text:

The regenerated synthetic package and fresh local AOGM export validate against schema hash `e0ebe02f52c1fb52e83ce6e91074d82f4adf5c39db7af8e7a7512dd83e5c3f62`; AOGM constructs 30 races, 30 castes, Human/Fighter at ID 1, and its normal party-setup session at land 0 coordinate 48,15.

The headless package-probe teardown warning was later traced to a strong `RealmzRules`/`CombatFlow` ownership cycle. CombatFlow now retains only the stateless rule modules it uses, the typed suite and package probe release cleanly, and the aggregate gate rejects future ObjectDB/resource-retention diagnostics. title: Current rolling fidelity pass — Special-57 combat healing and actor targeting
text:
## Current rolling fidelity pass — Special-57 combat healing and actor targeting

- Active-content inventory selected the narrow source-settled healing branch instead of treating all nonordinary spells alike. Remake supplied a dedicated healing adapter and stock-spell tests; Castle's manual picker, monster `getrange`, reflection, resistance, `resolvespell`, and `heal` establish the actual target and mutation rules.
- Player target-one spells now expose every living party or monster actor in Classic slot order rather than imposing a hostile-only UI rule. Strict combat special 57 resolves reflection and resistance first, then negates rolled damage. Party healing respects stone/death exclusions and maximum stamina; monster `cannot == 4` selects same-allegiance actors including self, may exceed maximum stamina, and retains Castle's otherwise surprising healed-monster attacked marker.
- Monster over-healing exposed a persistence-model defect: the loader had rejected current stamina above maximum even though Castle creates that state. Restore now accepts over-maximum values while retaining signed-16 bounds, and monster healing uses the shared signed arithmetic so an extreme result cannot create an unsaveable aggregate.
- Providence schema v2 already contains every required field, so no compiler change or package migration is needed. Spell resolution events carry both signed `damage` and positive `healing`; character/monster health, spell cost, active cast count, attacked state, and RNG restore through the existing save-v3 aggregate.
- The typed suite passes 2,413 assertions across 13 suites. Forty-one differential cases distinguish implemented special 57 from all other special and zero-damage branches.

Flagged rather than guessed: Castle special 60 appears to consume the shared damage value while some authored records may use duration fields; specials 58 through 60 need individual control-flow and active-content evidence. Providence currently emits generic `Realmz Spell <id>` names for standard spell records without project overrides. Camp healing is a separate application workflow. None of these is silently inherited from special 57.

Next rolling priority: correct the standard-spell display metadata at the Providence boundary, then inventory active specials 58 through 60 and class-nine effects by certified-campaign reachability before selecting another runtime branch.

title: Current rolling fidelity pass — Advanced character construction and vault publication
text:
## Current rolling fidelity pass — Advanced character construction and vault publication

- The Identity stage now offers Castle's fixed `Startlevel` choices—1, 3, 5, 7, 9, 11, 13, 15, 17, 20, 25, and 30—filtered only by the campaign maximum. The core builds the level-one base, sets prestige and the caste victory threshold, and invokes the ordinary level-up transaction once per additional level before starting spells and initial items. Presentation never synthesizes the advanced result.
- Providence commit `8f5fcf6830bee8249333c53c4da14b57e147e878` adds the previously missing fourteen-value race ability row, both caste ability rows, and thirty victory thresholds. The runtime mirror hash is `040f50ab9bd67a98a626176de876848b135fb449263fcd989664652a65bc7acd`; malformed lengths fail before content construction. The synthetic fixture was regenerated twice byte-identically and its positive/stale-hash pair now represents this contract.
- This pass caught two source-boundary defects before they became durable rules. Castle's level-up condition threshold replaces a nonnegative current value with permanent `-1`; it does not subtract one. Castle also loops across fifteen character trained-ability slots while the race/caste records author only fourteen. `FD-CHARACTER-001` keeps the unauthored slot zero and draw-free, and the runtime now keeps trained abilities separate from the twelve racial combat modifiers.
- The character's two-hand value is constructed, persisted, and displayed because Castle initializes and clamps it. No combat effect is inferred: the pinned attack source does not currently consume that field.
- Finalization now yields a typed, saveable yes/no publication decision. The session commits the new member before that request; acceptance emits a host event only after the interaction clears, and `RealmzApplication` publishes one immutable `.r2char` revision. Decline leaves the vault untouched. Stable character IDs may contain interior dots, but traversal components remain invalid.
- Godot MCP Pro exercised the fresh local AOGM package through a level-three Human Fighter roll, all five creator stages, party addition, the publication prompt, and a successful transactional vault write. The resulting current index points to a parseable immutable revision carrying level, campaign/package provenance, fifteen trained-ability values, and two-hand state. This walkthrough also caught and corrected stale Appearance guidance surviving onto the asynchronously populated Review page.
- The typed suite passes 2,662 assertions across 13 suites. Forty-four differential cases now include the aligned advanced creator and the named trained-ability boundary correction. Providence's focused 21 Rust tests, unit tests, typecheck, production build, and repeated deterministic export all pass.

Next application-workflow priority: complete package-backed portrait and combat-icon catalogs and the vault management workspace (revision history, archive, eligibility, and explicit publication feedback). Keep those media identities Providence-authored and Castle-adjudicated; do not guess filesystem assets or attach repository writes to ordinary gameplay.
