Victory awarded 1,842 experience per eligible living participant, advanced Brom Ascendant once to level 10, restored both the exact result request and the separate 18-point spell-selection request from saves, and confirmed the completed spell choice through the ordinary presenter.
- Tier 3 passed 3,981 assertions across twenty-two suites, teardown-leak rejection, all architecture/package/export gates, the 142-resource application-media manifest, 78 differential cases, and the 60-Classic/8-host inventory with one remaining host release blocker. Clean pinned Castle, Remake, and Providence references also passed external symbol validation. Source intelligence regenerated to 6,074 entities, 54,839 relationships, five flows, and 6,162 chunks.
- Godot MCP Pro completed the ordinary route, captured the live result/spell boundaries, confirmed return to exploration, and stopped the scene. Presentation remains functional rather than accepted, and ordinary total defeat, special battle modes 5/10, opcode 48 bonus treasure, and incidental reward quirks remain explicit—not inferred as complete.

Auto Weapon Switch now matches Castle's application-owned, default-on preference: only a qualifying manual projectile collision consults it, Guard resolves first, and the surviving actor switches once before the ordinary contact attack. The pending one-move decision survives interrupted Guard/age continuations without moving the preference itself into gameplay saves.

Next batch: certify the ordinary AOGM Camp/Rest, Pool/Share, denomination Swap, and contextual-service entry workflows before beginning another implementation tranche.

### Ordinary AOGM exploration and services certification closeout

- Ordinary AOGM play now covers the complete selected batch. Camp and Rest were previously observed through the field interface. A six-character party then pooled 1,305 gold, shared it as 218/218/218/217/217/217, and completed a five-gold character-to-pool-to-character Swap round trip without changing the total.
- The live money evidence is deliberately limited to gold. The selected AOGM party had no gems or jewelry, so those denominations retain synthetic coverage rather than being described as ordinary-play observations.
- The party reached an authored AOGM Temple action point through exploration. Its action sequence exposed both Temple and Bank as location services; entering Temple presented all nine fixed services plus Pool, Share, and Leave, and Leave returned cleanly to the field at the same location.
- This closes the contextual-service entry gap, but it does not certify the complete Temple workflow. No service purchase, no-op payment, or service-boundary reload was performed, so `GAP-SVC-004` remains the owning live-proof gap.
- No product code changed in this closeout. The workflow inventory and generated status report record only the variants observed through the ordinary application path.

## Current workflow batch — Session lifecycle and host responsiveness

- Validated save previews are complete: the System workspace indexes primary and backup records independently, shows detached identity/time/location/party facts, disables corrupt or mismatched records, and restores a selected validated source without mutating the active session on failure.
- End Adventure is now separate from Campaign Library and process Quit. Outside battle it offers explicit Save and end, End without saving, and Cancel operations; battle removes the save option. These labels are modern host copy rather than claimed Castle resource text. The host prompt is not gameplay state, noncombat gameplay interactions remain modal, save failure suppresses close, and `GameSession.close` releases the aggregate exactly once.
- `FD-APPLICATION-001` deliberately adds an outside-combat Cancel operation rather than reproducing Castle's ambiguous No-means-discard path. The application-hook pass now serializes and runs Castle's Global quit macro slot 2 through a saveable continuation. End Adventure remains synthetic until ordinary acceptance; scenario-owned Party Death integration remains a separate unresolved combat gap.
- Focused host-transaction tests prove save-before-close ordering, no-write discard, and no-op Cancel; save repository tests separately prove transactional write/readback. Full composition-root failure injection remains a named minor test gap rather than being described as verified persistence.
- Process Quit now remains distinct from End Adventure. Both the menu command and `NOTIFICATION_WM_CLOSE_REQUEST` use one host-owned typed confirmation; an active field session may save before quitting, battle cannot save, explicit no-save bypasses persistence, and Cancel or save failure leaves the process open. `FD-APPLICATION-002` records the safety correction from Castle's outside-combat No-means-quit behavior. Castle Quit never runs Global macro slot 2, so this workflow has no Providence dependency.
- Root-level notification and repository-failure proof remains pending until package discovery no longer blocks main-scene startup. This limitation is recorded as a minor test gap rather than treating pure host-transaction coverage as a live window-close result.
- Package discovery now inspects manifest/schema/capability metadata without hashing roughly 828 MB of installed payloads on the interactive frame. Choosing Play runs complete integrity validation and immutable installation in a host-owned worker, exposes detached determinate/indeterminate progress plus cooperative Cancel, and joins the worker during shutdown.
- The worker owns no Nodes or active-session state. The composition root consumes its result exactly once and changes package media only after a replacement session starts successfully, so rejection or failed session construction leaves the existing presentation catalog untouched.
- Focused package repository, worker, and presentation coverage proves structural discovery, deferred hash rejection, success/failure/cancellation, exact-once result handoff, clean join/teardown, and UI progress signaling.
- The MCP closeout selected the installed AOGM package through the ordinary campaign library. The application stayed queryable while complete validation ran, exposed Cancel, disabled competing Play actions, completed successfully once, and on a second run accepted cancellation without creating a session. The 960x600 frame was captured and the scene stopped cleanly. This closes the host validation-progress live-proof gap without claiming campaign-route certification.

Batch closeout: Tier 2 passed 1,017 focused assertions; Tier 3 passed 3,685 assertions across twenty-two suites, the aggregate architecture/package/export gates, 74 bidirectionally linked differential cases, and the 60-Classic/8-host inventory. Clean pinned Castle, Remake, and Providence references also passed external evidence validation. The next workflow batch is selected from the regenerated audit queue.

## Current workflow batch — Maps and Journal

- The batch owns three separate Castle workflows: player-authored location notes, discovered authored journal entries, and acquired player-map records. They must not share state merely because the modern shell presents them under one Journal route.
- Location notes are the first workflow. Castle stores them in separate land and dungeon record streams, preserves source-file order, permits editing only at the current party location, captures land darkness/torch state, clears the native record ID for empty text, and copies both streams with the playthrough save.

The modern non-mutating control is therefore labelled Revert draft rather than claiming Classic Cancel fidelity. - The second workflow reconstructs manual authored-journal discovery from Data SD2 identity. Positive Classic text can emit Take note through its existing saveable acknowledgement frame; discovered IDs persist in numeric source order and resolve immutable package text on view/restore. `FD-MAPS-002` bounds the table to IDs 0 through 2,999 rather than reproducing Castle's contradictory 5,999 cursor clamp. text:

Next application-workflow priority: use the remaining audit blocker and major-gap queue, with ordinary missile/defeat-or-retreat/level-up evidence and pointer-based spatial targeting scheduled as bounded combat follow-ups rather than reopening settled combat formulas.

- Camp remains a mode, not a fixed-duration heal. Entry clears contextual services and advances five source-scaled time clicks; explicit exit advances two. A separate typed Rest intent represents one held-control pulse, subtracting two fatigue before five time clicks so presentation repeat cadence cannot become simulation time.

- Land movement from camp commits fifteen time clicks before the requested move; dungeon movement commits two. Random rectangles are checked during that departure. An interrupting random battle retains a validated post-time continuation in combat state, survives save/reload and reward interactions, and resumes the requested move exactly once after battle return.

It performed an invented eight-hour full-heal transaction and could not truthfully represent either Castle's Camp command or held Rest loop. - The regenerated audit reports 60 Classic workflows, 8 host workflows, 1 blocker, 62 bidirectionally linked differential cases, and 36 functional Classic workflows. The earlier 38 count overcredited timed-event dispatch in both the clock and encounter workflows; correcting the denominator is evidence hygiene, not a product regression.

Flagged at this stage rather than copied: Castle adds its signed Poisoned condition value to half-day healing, its timed-encounter location code guards the y comparison with `recx`, and the `continueday` loop may repeat recovery around multiple records. ## Current rolling fidelity pass — Party Order

## Current rolling fidelity pass — Classic bank-backed Swap

- Castle does not implement banking as arbitrary gold deposits and withdrawals. Opcode 49 enables a location context; opening the ordinary Swap modal moves every banked gold, gem, and jewelry record into the shared pool once. Pool, Share, and character transfers retain their ordinary rules, and Done closes only the modal.

Responses may Pool, Share, transfer five gold or one gem/jewelry, or finish; the presenter owns no legality or mutation.

A source-legal location departure returns the complete remaining pool to the bank, clears the pool, and disables the contextual service exactly once.
- The same archaeology exposed a related shop defect: Castle shop entry imports all banked denominations and shop exit returns the complete remainder. The runtime now does both without changing the shop continuation or `.r2save` v3 envelope.
- Providence schema v2 needs no change. Opcode 49 is already compiled and all banked, pooled, and personal denominations are mutable session state.
- The later application-hook pass reclassifies Shop and Temple's contextual Global hooks as compiled and session-owned while retaining their ordinary-play and native empty-slot gaps. Bank-backed Swap remains functional from source, simulation, persistence, and presentation evidence; it is not certified because no ordinary campaign bank route has been exercised. Counts belong to the generated workflow report rather than this historical narrative.

Flagged rather than hidden: Castle's bank is visually the generic Swap modal, while 2.0 keeps a separately labelled Bank command for discoverability. This does not alter the source mutation sequence. Money-changing rates and ordinary-campaign bank acceptance remain separate workflow gaps; the no-bank pooled-wealth departure workflow is completed in the following pass.

Next batch priority: finish the coherent service-workflow closeout through one ordinary AOGM contextual service route, then return to the regenerated major-gap queue rather than reopening isolated economy formulas.

### Ordinary Swap lifecycle audio

- A deliberate ordinary Services-route entry now requests Castle's Swap-button sound 141, stops existing channels before modal sound 3003, and leaving that route through Done, Back, a menu, or a shortcut requests sound 141. Repeated rerenders and same-route mutations do not replay the sequence.

Realmz 2.0's default-audio sequence is source-shaped, but the preference itself is now tracked as `GAP-SYS-003` until modal sounds are comprehensively classified.

### No-bank pooled-wealth departure

- Castle resolves a nonempty no-bank money pool before destination passability. Realmz 2.0 now yields one save-owned yes/no warning for every valid direction, including a direction that will later be blocked; malformed directions still fail before opening the warning.
- The question requests Castle sound 20005 after stopping existing audio. Declining clears all three pooled denominations and resolves the original direction exactly once. Accepting opens typed Swap with sound 3003; Pool, Share, exact transfers, and their unavailable reasons remain core-owned.
- Done requests sound 141, clears any remaining pool, and resumes the saved ordinary movement exactly once. Declining does the same after clearing the pool. Warning, distribution, empty-pool, and post-transfer states restore transactionally through the existing `.r2save` v3 continuation envelope; forged directions, stale response IDs, and mismatched request payloads are rejected.
- `classic-pooled-wealth-departure-source-observation.json` records the pinned control flow. The exact STR# 135 question-6 wording is absent from the source tree, so the current prompt is explicitly synthetic and remains eligible for replacement by an authoritative resource/runtime observation.
- Providence schema v2 needs no change because this workflow consumes only mutable session state. Remake's one-entry warning/next-entry clearing behavior is recorded as divergent rather than ported.
- Castle's separate internal `moveparty` fallback returns before coordinate mutation after accepted distribution, but ordinary land and dungeon callers invoke `checkmoneypool` earlier and continue. The ordinary application workflow follows those callers rather than substituting the fallback.
- The audit now records `GAP-EXP-006`: Castle advances tile-specific time on several blocked land and dungeon attempts, while 2.0 currently publishes `movement_blocked` without that downstream time/random processing. That is a distinct major movement gap requiring its own archaeology and fixture.
- The regenerated audit reports 36 functional Classic workflows, 29 major gaps, one host release blocker, and 67 bidirectionally linked differential cases. The completed pooled-wealth variant remains inside Travel and Swap; Travel becomes partial because the newly evidenced blocked-time variant is unresolved.

This is the third focused workflow commit in the service/money batch. Batch closeout now requires one aggregate verification, one coherent MCP walkthrough, and one final source-intelligence regeneration.

## Current workflow batch — Classic information surfaces

- Completed pre-adventure character inspection across campaign setup and the vault. The setup shell now exposes the same detached character facts used by the active Character workspace without importing a character or mutating the session.
- Completed ordinary item inspection. Identified, unidentified, concealed-curse, and revealed-curse records present source-backed facts and restrictions; disabled actions expose their reasons directly. Castle's `iscurse` field is treated as the unworn decoy identity, while equipping reveals the original cursed record.
- Audited acquired player maps end to end and rejected the previous false implementation. Castle opcode 29 addresses `Data MD2` player-map records, not playable land levels. Providence parses those records but schema v2 does not export them, so 2.0 now fails with `player_map_contract_unavailable` without persisting a false acquired-map ID.
- The acquired-map workflow remains missing, with separate compiler and presentation gaps. Its follow-up must add names, picture/scrolling-text/crop modes, markers, notes, and exact media reachability across Providence and Realmz 2.0 before enabling opcode 29 or the Journal browser. Castle's apparent ID-20 acquisition-array overflow remains an explicit fidelity decision.
- The audit reports 60 Classic workflows, 8 host workflows, 38 functional Classic workflows, 28 major gaps, one host release blocker, and 68 bidirectionally linked differential cases. The map workflow's move from partial to missing is a corrected denominator, not a product regression.
- The risk-tiered method was applied as intended: each workflow received focused Tier 2 verification and its own commit; the three-workflow batch scheduled the aggregate suite, source-intelligence regeneration, clean-reference validation, and MCP walkthrough only at closeout. Bounded archaeology was delegated where suitable, while fidelity adjudication, integration, and final status remained Sol-owned.
- The first MCP walkthrough found the Equipment heading's slot count collapsing into a one-character column at 960×600. A bounded presenter repair reserves proportional width for heading details, adds a regression assertion, and passed the policy's one post-repair Tier 3 rerun plus a second visual walkthrough. ## Current rolling fidelity pass — Timed midnight encounters

- Crossing midnight now owns an ordered, serializable timed-encounter scan. Matching records advance their effective day before the chance draw and item, quest, level, rectangle, and coordinate gates; eligible records enter the ordinary scenario VM and resume the remaining scan after each typed interaction.
- Midnight health and ration recovery is deferred until timed eligibility has been evaluated. It commits once before the first dispatched record or once after a scan with no dispatch, and its cleared pending flag survives save/restore so an acknowledgement cannot replay healing or consume another ration.
- `FD-EXPLORATION-001` corrects Castle's y-field guard and inconsistent movement-location globals to the semantic attempted/current/committed party coordinate. `FD-EXPLORATION-002` corrects Castle's `continueday` loop, which can repeat half-day recovery once per eligible record.

- Providence schema v2 already preserves all required timed fields and source order, so this pass changes no package contract. Focused tests cover chance failure, exact gates, day mutation, event/RNG order, staged text, one-time recovery, and interaction save/resume.
- The regenerated audit reports 60 Classic workflows, 8 host workflows, 39 functional Classic workflows, one host blocker, and 70 bidirectionally linked differential cases. Timed variants and Camp/Rest are functional, while the encounter workflow remains partial for location-changing AP destination proof.

Flagged rather than copied: Castle's successful land path checks one tile beyond the committed destination, dungeon time checks the pre-move floor, y-only requirements can be skipped, and multiple eligible records can multiply healing. The first three coordinate artifacts and repeated recovery are named corrections; fatigue and torch behavior are resolved in the subsequent hourly-clock pass.

### Poisoned half-day recovery

- Complete Castle control flow resolves the apparently suspicious signed term without a runtime correction. `reduce()` first damages the character by the positive Poisoned value and decrements that value; noon or midnight recovery then adds the remaining value to the ordinary level-based recovery. Across the complete boundary, Poisoned therefore changes the result to base recovery minus one rather than granting extra health.
- The existing clock implementation already preserves that order. A source-shaped regression now proves pre-decay damage, post-decay recovery, event ordering, and the resulting unchanged health for a level-six unrationed character with Poisoned 3.
- No package, save, RNG, VM, or presentation contract changed. `classic.exploration.camp-rest` is now functional from source, simulation, persistence, presentation, and ordinary AOGM evidence; the broader clock workflow is completed in the following hourly fatigue/light pass.

### Hourly fatigue and light

- Castle's `if (timeclick)` expression is a function-symbol typo and therefore always true, but it sits inside the genuine hour-crossing branch. Its observable result is simply one bounded fatigue point per hour, which 2.0 already preserved.
- Torch Lit is deliberately reduced in both the generic party-condition loop and a second torch-specific branch. Combined with light special 50's `30 * power - 1` initialization and darkness bands, this is a distinct two-point hourly duration scale rather than an accidental duplicate generic condition tick. Realmz 2.0 now matches it without allowing the final one-point value to become negative.
- Castle can leave stale incremental torch art when a value of two reaches zero because its redraw flag is captured before both decrements. Realmz 2.0 does not copy this presentation artifact: detached light state reaches zero once and disposable presentation caches rebuild from that truth.
- Focused source-order tests cover values three, two, and one, expiration event cardinality, the ordinary Rest hour boundary, and fatigue ordering. The regenerated audit reports 40 functional Classic workflows and 71 bidirectionally linked differential cases; `classic.exploration.time-fatigue-light` is now functional.

### Exploration cadence batch closeout

- Closed four adjacent workflows under the risk-tiered policy: blocked positive land-attempt timing, timed-midnight dispatch and continuation, poisoned half-day recovery, and hourly fatigue/light decay. Each landed as a focused-verified commit before the batch gate.
- Tier 3 passed 3,512 assertions across all 20 typed suites, architecture and export-contract checks, teardown-leak rejection, 71 differential cases, and the complete 60-Classic/8-host workflow inventory. Clean pinned-reference validation also passed. Providence was unchanged, so no compiler gate was required.
- Godot MCP Pro opened the current 960×600 fixture shell, inspected the scene, played the main scene, and accepted input. Its runtime-tree and screenshot bridge timed out; Windows Graphics Capture completed the visual fallback. The ordinary UI created a character through all five steps, entered exploration, and advanced Camp/Rest from 00:00 to 00:25 to 00:50 without overlap or inaccessible controls. The editor log contained no runtime errors after stop.
- The current audit reports 40 functional Classic workflows, one host release blocker, and 71 bidirectionally linked differential cases. This visual evidence is a synthetic fixture walkthrough, not ordinary AOGM certification.

Next batch priority: use the regenerated audit queue to choose 3–5 adjacent application workflows. Preserve the unresolved movement/Swap observations—ordinary callers continue movement after distribution, while the direct `moveparty(1)` fallback returns—and settle them only in the dedicated source-backed workflow that owns movement resumption.

## Current workflow batch — AOGM combat feedback and command parity

- The workflow inventory now schedules battle entry, tactical movement, physical attacks, combat casting, and manual turn control as the active batch. Auto Turn, persistent character Auto, Delay, Bandage, Turn Undead, and Undo are separate workflows rather than hidden variants of one oversized turn-control record. The previous exploration/services certification targets retain their evidence in the queue.
- Batch 1 adds a presentation-owned combat playback transaction over the previous detached view, ordered committed events, and final detached view. Movement, melee, ordinary projectiles, spell cast/projectile/eight-frame resolution, fixed result numbers, defeat settlement, and ordered sounds cannot mutate or advance simulation. Space skips only visuals; reduced motion collapses the visual path while preserving audio.
- Battlefield-native targeting replaces coordinate spin boxes. Actor and repeated-actor selection uses core-provided combatant identities; area selection previews exact Data AD offsets only at core-provided legal centers. Cancel emits no response, while confirmation preserves the existing combat response ABI.
- The integrated application-media catalog now includes proven combat CIcon families in addition to all 142 Classic sounds. Exact scenario keys still override application keys. CIcon 161 is not called blood or gore, CIcon 167 lacks a traced caller, and death-effect timing remains unresolved rather than being presented as settled fidelity.
- Providence schema v2 already preserves `lookStart`, `lookEnd`, spell sounds, and scenario CIcon overrides, so this batch requires no package-contract change. Automated evidence may make these workflows functional, but acceptance and certification still require the ordinary AOGM MCP route and user review.

### Source-backed combat commands

- The follow-on command tranche implements five separately audited workflows: current-turn Auto, persistent character Auto, Delay, Bandage, and Turn Undead. Availability and disabled reasons come from the detached combat view; the command deck and roster submit only stable IDs and typed actions.
- Persistent Auto is save-owned, survives battles, and starts the active character immediately when enabled. Both Auto forms share one deterministic rules routine and stop at manual, mandatory, error, or terminal boundaries. State and RNG roll back together at the bounded operation limit.
- `FD-COMBAT-012` advances a last-slot Delay to the next round instead of reproducing Castle's duplicate-activation cursor artifact. `FD-COMBAT-013` exposes one actual living bleeding recipient instead of Castle's broad manual picker. Turn Undead preserves source target order, signed sentinel, RNG, experience, result effects, and death-macro continuation.
- The inventory now reports 46 functional Classic workflows and 91 bidirectionally linked differential cases. These command workflows remain certification targets until the integrated command deck and reachable variants receive ordinary AOGM evidence.

### Bounded Undo and remaining command parity

- Undo is not a generic state rollback. The save aggregate records only the active character, activation-start cell, round, turn index, and availability. Result-free movement retains the boundary; attacks, spells, item effects, reactions, and turn advancement invalidate it.
- The source-backed ordinary path restores an empty start cell, applies Castle's attack-allocation adjustment, recalculates movement and attacks, requests sounds 664 then ordinary activation 138, and presents the reverse step without advancing simulation.
- `FD-COMBAT-014` rejects an occupied activation-start cell instead of reproducing Castle's unchecked field overwrite. Repeated Undo and first/last-slot or round-boundary re-entry remain explicit runtime-fixture work rather than being guessed from the global cursor.
- The active batch has closed combat scroll use and numeric Fast Spell shortcuts; it next owns Auto Weapon Switch as a host preference translated into an explicit typed combat choice. That interface is not inferred from the existing charged-item, weapon-mode, or persistent-Auto contracts.
