# Deterministic Realmz core contract

## Purpose

Own the pure Realmz model, fixed Classic rules, topology, game clock, randomness, and complete session state.

## Ownership

- Direct Realmz definitions and mutable playthrough state, including characters, equipment, wealth, conditions, encounters, battles, shops, treasures, spells, monsters, races, and castes.
- `GameSession`, typed intents/events/interactions/views, and snapshot boundaries.
- `RealmzRules`, `RealmzClock`, `RealmzRng`, topology queries, and world overlays.

## Local Contracts

- All classes are pure `RefCounted` or value-like data. They never extend or retain Nodes.
- Rule modules may retain the smaller rule dependencies they use, but may not strongly retain their owning `RealmzRules` aggregate; core ownership graphs must remain acyclic so headless and host teardown release complete sessions.
- No scenes, autoloads, filesystem/resource APIs, audio, OS services, wall-clock time, or Godot randomness.
- JSON dictionaries stop at validating infrastructure factories. Domain state is typed and does not expose writable backing dictionaries.
- Classic option-label records are immutable typed content distinct from ordinary messages; runtime choice resolution may query them but never mutate their source table.
- Every gameplay mutation is committed synchronously by `GameSession`.
- `GameSession` owns scenario execution state and is the only object allowed to connect VM operations to domain mutations.
- Session state owns encounter attempts/type flags, equipment escrow, mutable base-shop quantities, normalized buyback stock, combat, and scenario-program replacement. These are save data, never mutations of installed package definitions.
- Session state owns the selected Classic difficulty and Monster Set from party setup. Difficulty uses Castle's five signed choices; party commitment freezes the source-authored experience multiplier, while money continues to use the saved difficulty multiplier. Monster Set resolves every constructed monster through the package's complete typed replacement catalog. New sessions deliberately reset both choices to Normal instead of preserving Castle's stale process globals.
- Combat state owns the active actor's action, retained target, and next authored monster attack row. Its nonterminal outcome sentinel is the explicit `active` value; an empty outcome is not an active-battle test. Character attack capacity remains a signed integer half-unit field on `CharacterState`; save/resume may not recompute or round either boundary.
- Session state owns non-VM interaction continuations as well as VM continuations. Random-rectangle surprise choices serialize with their owning region and resume only through `GameSession.respond`.
- Start Game, Party Death, End Adventure, contextual Shop, and contextual Temple execute as package-owned application hooks through the session VM. Their exact hook identity, program, resume operation, service identity, revival result, pending request, and VM frame form one save-v3 continuation. Direct scenario Shop and Temple opcodes bypass the contextual service hooks.
- Live age-band changes yield ordered `age_update` requests. Movement clock work suspends a post-clock continuation whose nested resume remains the unstarted post-move operation, so age acknowledgement and any midnight timed scan precede destination AP discovery. Each typed response advances one character before the owning session operation resumes.
- Monster death macros execute before battle resolution. Their combatant identity, VM interaction, and direct-session continuation belong to the save aggregate and resume only through `GameSession.respond`. Monsters killed by one spell enqueue death macros in source target order; combat state owns the queue, original caster, and deferred turn decision, validates the exact completion cursor, and drains every macro before battle outcome or caster advancement.
- Direct session-owned total-party defeat runs the Party Death hook before aggregate release. Opcode 119 revival records a no-reward retreat, publishes one terminal battle return, and releases combat exactly once without closing the session. Scenario-VM-owned battle defeat still requires an explicit suspension/resumption design before this behavior can be claimed for every battle caller; Castle's callers do not all take the same post-revival `booty` path.
- A placed Action Point's Classic header is a post-action map/coordinate destination. `GameSession` applies it only after that AP completes, rechecks the destination cell once, and serializes the recheck depth so save/resume cannot repeat or skip it.
- An ordinary placed Action Point becomes disabled after its complete timeline. Classic opcode 24 Keep Codes preserves it; opcode 25 may disable it explicitly. This world-overlay state is serialized across every interaction and save boundary.
- Every gameplay random draw goes through the session-owned `RealmzRng` and is serializable.
- Each character owns exactly ten Fast Spell bindings. A binding stores one known stable spell ID and valid power, persists inside character state across campaign saves and vault revisions, and invokes the ordinary field/combat cast contracts; shortcut activation may not duplicate cost, target, RNG, or effect rules. `FD-SPELL-003` permits exact-cost activation and commits only after valid targeting instead of reproducing Castle's prepayment and greater-than-or-equal cost defects.
- `RealmzRng` uses the documented QuickDraw 16807/mod-2147483647 state transition and Castle's inclusive scaling; raw scripted values are test-only branch controls.
- Snapshots and restores detach typed state so callers cannot mutate an active session through a prior envelope.
- `GameSession.close` releases the complete aggregate exactly once at an ordinary or active-combat command boundary and publishes only detached campaign identity. Other gameplay interactions remain modal and reject close transactionally. Host confirmation and repository writes remain outside the simulation; a closed session has no save envelope or pending interaction.
- `MapTopology` plus `WorldState` overlays is the only source for simulation map facts; movement, pathfinding, LOS, search, triggers, and views reuse its explicit cells, edges, and features.
- Player-authored location notes are mutable `WorldState` records, separate from immutable acquired-player-map definitions and scenario-authored journal discovery. They preserve independent land/dungeon record streams, stable source ordinals, map level/location, native location ID, and Castle's saved darkness value. Only the party's current validated topology cell may be changed. `FD-MAPS-001` rejects a 502nd record per stream rather than reproducing Castle's append-beyond-search defect; editing consumes no clock or RNG.
- Authored-journal discovery is mutable `GameState`, not copied narrative text or a chronological event log. It stores unique Data SD2 message IDs 0 through 2,999, detaches their immutable package text in numeric source order, consumes no clock or RNG, and validates every identity against content before restore. `FD-MAPS-002` rejects Castle's unsafe 5,999 cursor range rather than indexing beyond its 3,000 saved flags; browsing position remains presentation-only.
- Acquired player maps are immutable `WorldDefinition` records plus stable acquired IDs in `WorldState`. Detached views expose all twenty menu slots in source order, but attach topology cells, exact media IDs, markers, notes, and current-party eligibility only to acquired records. `FD-MAPS-003` rejects IDs outside zero through nineteen and nonpositive icon sizes before either value can reach Castle's unsafe array/division paths. Viewing remains presentation-owned and consumes no time or RNG.
- Land travel accepts all eight adjacent destination cells, follows diagonal Layout neighbors at map corners, and charges the destination tile's ordinary movement cost. Direct movement, detached availability, and land pathfinding use the same destination probe without corner blocking. Dungeon movement and pathfinding remain cardinal and edge-based.
- A topology cell retains immutable presentation metadata for its base tileset/tile and optional special-land overlay asset. These facts pass through detached views but never become an alternate movement, LOS, or trigger model.
- Immutable `BattleTerrainSetDefinition` catalogs preserve Castle's signed mapstats and exact 3×3 combat builds for battlefield construction. They are map-referenced construction inputs, not a second exploration topology. Battle start generates one session-owned `BattlefieldState` from the current map plus overlays before initiative; terrain, source shifts, actor anchors, positions, and complete footprints serialize with `CombatState`, while `BattlefieldView` is detached presentation data.
- Battlefield setup follows Castle's terrain-decoration, formation, party, ally, authored-slot, monster-construction, dead-position cleanup, and initiative order. It is transactional. `FD-COMBAT-006` requires a complete finite placement search and exact state/RNG rollback when no legal cell or footprint exists; no setup failure may leave speculative draws or partial combat state.
- Random rectangles follow Castle's reverse region order, 1-in-10,000 chance scale, three ordered random-door draws, signed one-shot door state, surprise choice, and battle selection through the session RNG.
- A moved-to coordinate selects only its lowest `classic_record_index` placed Action Point. Disabled or failed selected records do not fall through to another same-cell AP; positive sub-100 chances consume one tagged draw, while percentages below one consume none.
- `GameView` and its map/cell views are detached read models for presentation and never expose mutable simulation objects.
- Combat rules publish detached, non-save-owned presentation facts in ordered domain events: source actor/target coordinates, semantic result kind and amount, and exact proven Classic effect resource identities. These facts describe an already committed mutation; they never create a playback continuation or allow animation to advance the turn. Spatial spell options also expose the complete rules-owned legal center set so presentation does not repeat range, LOS, mask, or battlefield-boundary calculations.
- Detached item/spell/monster views carry exact content icon IDs and resource types. Item views retain player-visible item type and icon while revealing identified names, descriptions, definition identity, and values only after simulation marks the instance identified.
- Each detached carried-item view owns source-probed Equip, Unequip, Use, Identify, Split, Join, Drop, and exact Trade-target availability. Ordinary equip/unequip/trade/drop mutation goes through `InventoryRules`; presentation cannot infer slots, race/class admission, hands, quivers, curses, capacity, or load. `FD-INVENTORY-001` permits an equipped ordinary item to transfer as unequipped while blocking Castle's equipped-curse bypass and stale derived bonuses. Drop uses a save-owned yes/no continuation naming the exact character and item instance. Charged spell-item use validates the exact owner/instance, permission, context, charge, spell, power, and target before mutation; positive charges remove their per-charge load, negative charges remain infinite, and a pending field target selection plus rolled random field power are session/save-owned. Restore rejects a fixed-power continuation that does not match the item's authored power, and request text retains the player-known identified or unidentified item name. Combat item use spends Castle's movement/half-attack resources but no spell points. Paid identification is available only through an active shop service continuation; door/XAP items, scrolls, random-power combat staging, spatial/repeated combat item targets, field identification, unsupported passive effects, and Castle's contradictory split/join load path stay disabled until their own source-backed implementations or fidelity decisions exist.
- `EconomyRules` owns Classic shop buy and sale valuation. Sale integer-halves absolute cost, applies charge condition, caps sale inflation at 100 percent, and applies the unidentified one-fiftieth penalty. `FD-ECONOMY-001` treats a zero-authored-charge item as full condition instead of reproducing Castle's undefined zero-divided-by-zero conversion.
- `EconomyRules` also owns ordinary Pool, Share, and Swap probes and mutations. Pool removes all personal denomination load; Share processes jewelry, gems, then gold in party order; Swap moves exactly five gold or one gem or jewelry per action. Bank-backed Swap imports every banked denomination once on entry, leaves the pool untouched on Done, and returns the complete remainder to the bank when movement clears location services. Without a bank, a valid movement attempt with pooled wealth owns a typed saveable direction/choice continuation before passability: decline clears the pool, while accept opens Swap and Done clears the remainder; both resume that ordinary movement exactly once. Castle's distinct internal fallback return is not the ordinary caller contract. Bank-backed shops and temples import and return the same complete pool at their source exit boundary. Every committed wealth distribution recalculates Classic movement. `FD-ECONOMY-003` requires the complete denomination weight to fit instead of reproducing Share's jewelry-overload defect.
- `TempleRules` owns the nine fixed temple services and their signed percentage costs. Temple payment and Pool/Share mutation remain session-owned through `EconomyRules`; presentation receives prices, status, and exact availability but never applies healing, conditions, equipment, abilities, or wealth.
- Personal carried load is a derived invariant: gold plus gems plus fifteen times jewelry plus every item's base and charge weight from immutable package definitions. Character finalization materializes identified starting items with authored charges in caste order, tries ordinary Classic equipment admission, and retains only records that pass capacity. Vault import recomputes the total against the target package; save restore rejects unknown item identities or a mismatched total transactionally.
- Opcode 36 equipment escrow is scenario-owned party state, not a player storage service. Do not expose `PartyState` escrow or interim-find storage as an ordinary inventory destination.
- `GameView` reports action availability as `enabled` plus an explicit reason. Presenters cannot infer availability from the existence of a control. Combat Move availability derives from enabled detached `CombatView` movement probes while outcome is `active`; a fresh activation with no active turn transaction probes and displays the character's maximum movement even if committed state retains the prior remainder. The same active boundary suppresses exploration Move/Search and field item/spell actions.
- `MapView` carries a bounded 25×25 party-local cell projection, the complete visited-coordinate set needed by the minimap, and movement availability computed through the same topology query as movement: eight directions on land and four in dungeons. It does not duplicate the full 90×90 map for every presentation revision.
- Classic-visible Realmz behavior is the fixed ruleset. Fidelity corrections require a documented decision and source/oracle tests.
- Campaign display metadata, restriction summaries, race/caste eligibility, and character-creation drafts are detached read models. They may explain a legal choice, but only `GameSession` and fixed Classic rules decide whether a character can enter a party.
- Character appearance definitions are immutable package content with distinct portrait and combat-icon roles. Creation and vault import validate stable IDs against those roles; `FD-CHARACTER-002` aliases Human set zero to portrait 257/tactical 9000 rather than exposing missing source-formula resources.
- Party setup begins empty and remains session-owned across any number of finalized-character, vault-import, removal, save, and restore boundaries. Exploration intents fail until explicit Begin commits a nonempty party; no placeholder character or view-revision shortcut may stand in for that state.
- Active Party Order is one synchronous `PartyState` permutation of every current stable character ID exactly once. It preserves the existing character objects, consumes no RNG or clock time, and persists through the aggregate character array. Setup, solo-party, pending-interaction, and combat requests remain unavailable; malformed permutations are transactional failures. `FD-CHARACTER-003` makes cancellation presentation-owned instead of reproducing Castle's apparent cleared-track out-of-bounds write.
- Character generation commits one session-owned provisional `CharacterState` after the complete creation RNG sequence. Review, reroll, cancel, starting-spell edits, unspent-point confirmation, final acceptance, and vault-publication confirmation all preserve that boundary; accepting a reviewed character never rolls it again. The provisional state has no starting inventory; final acceptance grants identified, authored-charge caste items after spell selection and derives personal load, matching `CharacterGen`'s `addinitialitems` order without reproducing its premature `numitems` increment.
- Starting-spell selection follows Castle's seven costs and only the first twelve `cspells` slots per eligible level. Resource-name slots thirteen through fifteen are not character spells. Unspent points require a typed, saveable yes/no confirmation.
- Advanced creation accepts only Castle's fixed `Startlevel` choices through the campaign maximum. It constructs the level-one base, applies the target-minus-one prestige penalty and caste victory threshold, then invokes the ordinary level-up path once for every additional level before spells and initial items. Every registration, combat-stat, condition, spell-point, stamina, resistance, and ability draw remains in the session RNG trace.
- Character creation initializes all forty condition slots from the race, then applies only caste condition-level `1` as permanent `-1`; larger caste values are level-up thresholds. When reached, a threshold replaces a nonnegative current value with permanent `-1`; only an already-negative sentinel decrements. Initial saves use the serialized race/caste bonuses and the `CharacterState` `-99…120` bounds.
- `CharacterState.specials` owns twelve racial combat modifiers. Its separate fifteen-slot trained-ability array uses fourteen authored race/caste inputs; `FD-CHARACTER-001` keeps the unauthored final slot zero and draw-free. Two-hand is retained as a source-owned character statistic but has no inferred combat effect.
- Character creation preserves Castle's complete random sequence: six assigned attribute rolls plus the seventh discarded loop roll, gender adjustment, cumulative race aging rows through the caste minimum age group, final race/caste bounds, three threshold-based special bonuses, stamina, age, and optional spell points. Aging table columns 8 through 14 adjust only saves 0 through 6 during creation.
- Character inspection is detached and mutation-free. `CharacterView` owns named display projections for conditions, saves, special modifiers, abilities, race/caste traits, and all five aging rows; an active row is derived from age without reproducing Castle's view-time `currentagegroup` write under `FD-CHARACTER-004`. Lifetime prestige remains unavailable until every source counter has explicit state and mutation ownership.
- `CharacterState` persists exact age days and the independent current age group. Each crossed midnight and each source-backed age-changing spell invokes one Castle age operation: it may apply or erase only one adjacent row, does not reuse creation bounds, floors maximum movement at two, and adjusts only saves 0 through 6. Maximum age reduces battle experience to Castle's truncated two-thirds share; `doesNotDie` remains stored content but has no invented death or exemption behavior.
- A party-target monster attack with Classic special 17 consumes the generic special-potency draw after ordinary damage, tests save slot seven, and on failure applies the attack-row lifespan formula through the same one-transition aging rule. A changed band pauses combat at a session-owned age update before the next actor; the combat continuation, interaction, character mutation, pending weapon condition, Dragon Hide feedback, damage, and RNG boundary all survive save/restore and resume once in source order.
- Monster status specials 1 through 7 and 16 consume generic potency before their source-family save and mutate the exact Classic condition slot. A negative duration is permanent. Party targets add once only when the starting duration is below 30; monster targets stack without that gate. A monster target above 100 runtime magic resistance converts the complete special attack to a miss after potency and before its save. Special and source-sound events precede ordinary damage feedback.
- Monster resource specials 8 and 9 consume the same generic potency draw before their source-family branch. Spell drain tests save six, transfers up to three points per attacker hit die, and permits the attacker balance to exceed its maximum; experience drain tests save five, subtracts twenty times attacker maximum stamina from direct earned experience, and has no monster-target case. Both mutations and above-maximum monster spell energy remain session-owned and saveable.
- A source-shaped combat spell special 57 uses ordinary actor targeting, reflection, and resistance before healing. Party healing observes stone/death exclusions and caps at maximum health. Monster `cannot == 4` selects same-allegiance actors including self; monster healing retains signed-16 arithmetic, may leave current health above maximum, and marks that monster attacked. Restore validates signed bounds but may not reject this source-valid over-maximum state.
- Monster charm is battle allegiance, not a generic condition: save zero includes party charm resistance; affected party actors are session-owned automatic combatants, target only the opposite side, remain valid hostile targets for loyal actors, participate in outcome checks, survive mid-battle restore, and return to base allegiance at battle cleanup.
- Monster construction copies all forty immutable Data MD starting conditions into session-owned state before combat. Negative permanent values remain active; no constructor may synthesize or discard authored condition slots.
- Monster elemental specials 11 through 15 retain the generic potency draw followed by elemental damage, source-family save, and matching protection. `FD-COMBAT-001` consistently applies protection to committed monster-target damage instead of preserving Castle's cold-through-mental display-only ordering defect.
- Character melee resolves from a validated snapshot of equipped immutable definitions. Armed state comes only from an equipped Classic type-2 item, never from a nonzero damage bonus; conflicting melee slots fail explicitly. `FD-COMBAT-002` makes weapon elemental damage use the defender's save while retaining Castle's immunity, protection, and RNG order. Monster `requiredWeapon` and `magicToHit` are independent attack gates; battle `distance` is placement-only. `FD-COMBAT-003` normalizes specific signed-byte requirements to Divinity Item Numbers and disallows Castle's unarmed family-restriction bypass.
- Ordinary monster melee receives a detached attack context containing the resolved carried weapon, Realmz day, effective defender luck/armor, and party Dragon Hide state. Its bounded fumble-disabled resolver preserves Castle's luck-before-hit and weapon/unarmed damage order, evil-conditional protection, ten-percent floor, typed weapon gates, and Dragon Hide's physical-only reduction plus synchronous sound 694. `FD-COMBAT-004` floors negative physical damage at zero instead of allowing Castle's subtraction to heal the defender. `FD-COMBAT-010` replaces a projectile weapon from the actual attacker's native slot zero instead of Castle's stale global monster; reflection remains unavailable. Castle's positive `behind` is a withdrawal-attack modifier, not character/monster icon facing.
- Battle state owns a bounded twenty-entry queue of exact fumbled `ItemInstance` values and the active turn's committed-physical-action fact. Character attacks consume the level-scaled fumble draw even while unarmed; cursed weapons and a full queue suppress the fumble without changing the attack result. Armed monsters consume the HD-scaled draw, clear only their active weapon on a fumble, and continue later authored rows unarmed. Body-count selection precedes typed one-item recovery; `FD-COMBAT-005` preserves remaining charges. The fixed runtime currently uses Castle's default enabled behavior; do not add an `allowfumble` toggle without also source-owning its five-percent XP coupling.
- `ClassicRewardState` owns one bounded ordinary reward transaction: origin, source identity, exact pending instances, pooled experience and recipient awards, detection/identification knowledge, completion confirmation, level cursor/result, and spell-selection cursor. It must round-trip canonical JSON without accepting fractional integer fields. Battle state separately owns exact-once `rewards_started` and `rewards_completed` facts; package validation must finish before either reward RNG or that one-shot ownership advances.
- Treasure capacity uses the exact current `ItemInstance` weight and permits a result equal to maximum load under `FD-ECONOMY-002`. Presentation receives the core-owned availability/reason and may not recreate Castle's inconsistent base-weight strict-less-than check.
- Player-controlled character melee activations normalize any positive prior reserve to one half-unit, clear a negative reserve, add normal attacks plus attack bonus, add Castle's four Speedy half-units, and spend two units plus three movement per attempt. A reserve of at least two retains the active actor. Monster physical activations choose once, retain a living target, and execute each validated authored row in order. Charmed-character cadence, spell/item limits, monster Speedy overflow, and Castle's contradictory zero/one-unit display remain unresolved rather than sharing this bounded rule implicitly.
- Battle state owns each party character's Castle melee/missile toggle. Setup prefers an equipped type-2 weapon, otherwise type 15; switching costs no attacks, movement, turn, or RNG and returning to melee permits hand-to-hand. Equipment projection rejects duplicate type-2/type-10/type-15 slots. Missile mode cannot enter the melee resolver.
- Ordinary physical class-nine projectiles use integer-truncated Euclidean anchor range, the battlefield LOS query, projectile-shield immunity, missile dodge, one damage roll reused across fixed repeated hits, and one player caste-bonus draw. A committed player Fire spends one finite charge, two half-attacks, and twelve movement; a monster uses exact native slot one, retains initial range power while lowering unaffordable cost power, resolves at power one, spends all movement, clears Guard, and targets an opposed party character. Out-of-range or zero-affordable-power missiles continue into the source-ordered cast/movement decision without repeating the missile roll. Random-power, elemental, special, charmed-character, and allied-monster projectile paths remain explicit unavailable boundaries. Monster spell definitions preserve ten native positions; only a wholly empty legacy package array may normalize to ten empty slots, while any one-to-nine-entry array remains invalid because it can change slot selection and RNG.
- Ordinary memorized combat spells cover combat-enabled, non-projectile damage spells without specials. Player admission uses one mutation-free probe shared by the detached picker and execution, including Castle's flags, conditions, round-hit state, per-activation limit, known spell, cost, tier, range, and LOS. Monster casting samples exact fixed slots, retains initial range power while lowering affordability power, samples native target space, can issue multiple magical attacks, clears Guard/movement, and owns one persisted post-movement retry. Failed charm saves continue through Castle's later defenses. Friendly/charmed-monster, class-nine, special, item/fast/random-power, zero-damage, and anomalous nonpositive-cost branches remain explicit.
- Ordinary player automatic-group spells support target types 9, 10, and 12. They select living positioned party slots before monster slots, spend cost and action resources once, roll duration/base damage once, apply defenses per target, and enqueue defeated monster macros in that order. Monster group casting remains disabled because Castle bypasses current power/resource setup; target type 11 is not folded into this contract.
- Ordinary player spatial spells support target types 3 and 4. `SpellAreaRules` owns the eighteen source-ordered Data AD masks; fixed areas use the authored size and power areas use cast power. One typed battlefield center is range/LOS checked, intersecting footprints are deduplicated, over-100 monster resistance is removed during targeting, and party slots resolve before monster slots under one cost/duration/base-damage transaction. A mask that crosses the validated 90x90 field is rejected instead of reproducing Castle's unsafe indexing. Target type 0 remains a separate repeated-selection transaction. Reflection, authored adjacent-mask rotation, and queued persistent fields remain explicitly unavailable; both player and monster paths must reject queued fields rather than silently omit them.
- Ordinary size-zero target type 0 is an ordered repeated-selection transaction. A player chooses one through power distinct positioned actors, including self or either allegiance, pays once at chosen power, and rerolls duration/base damage for each selection. Monsters roll separate range/target power and sample opposed actors through Castle's native party/gap/monster slot space; they may commit fewer unique targets than paid power after exhausting one cast's hundred-attempt guard. `FD-COMBAT-011` prevents Castle's local retry counter from leaking into later casts, while retaining partial resolution and full chosen-power cost within a genuinely exhausted cast; the guard is not save state. For ordinary target types zero and one, each originally selected reflector consumes one 33-percent draw before duration/damage, redirects once to the active caster, and retains both selected and effective target identity. An unreflected over-100 monster consumes that repeated selection's pre-resolution rolls but receives no effect. A monster killed by its own reflected cast retains its battlefield anchor, completes the authored magic-attack count, then enters the serialized death-macro continuation. Castle's record-based queue may contain the same dead caster more than once; occupancy remains until that subject's final queued record completes, and the queue is bounded to Castle's 100 records. Nonzero-size open-space placement remains explicit.
- `BattlefieldRules` is the single owner for tactical footprint adjacency, deterministic LOS, projectile range/target legality, and one-step legality. Party movement accepts eight directions, validates the complete destination footprint, and never mutates turn resources on rejection. An opposed occupied destination remains an enabled directional command: Guard resolves first, then ordinary melee spends three movement and two half-attack units without moving; open movement instead charges the maximum destination terrain time plus changed axes. A manual missile-mode collision may carry the host's default-on Auto Weapon Switch decision only when the equipped type-15 item has `sp2 > 1100` and resolves to spell class nine plus damage type nine. That one-move decision survives an interrupted Guard continuation, switches to melee or hand-to-hand after Guard, plays sound 141, and performs exactly one ordinary contact attack. Direct attacks and automatic actors never consult the host preference. `CombatState` owns Guard flags plus the source-ordered, serializable pre-move Guard, fixed-origin withdrawal, committed-move, destination-Guard cursor, and living characters who explicitly left battle; interruption by age update, Escape confirmation, or a reviving death macro resumes without replay. Explicit Escape uses integer Euclidean range, Castle's condition/allegiance gates, per-character removal, and the exact 200 prestige penalty. Edge movement prompts or forces Escape before collision gates. Ordinary monsters retain or source-select one visible target, consume exact bounded `shift.c` retries, move through repeated complete-footprint probes, resolve party/allied Guard at contact, and attack only after adjacency; RUNS_AWAY monsters instead move away from their retained target, receive withdrawal attacks, and leave at the edge. Physical attacks, reactions, successful ordinary monster missiles, and successful ordinary monster spells clear monster Guard. Fixed-power combat scrolls reuse typed spell targeting and effects without spell-point or spell-attack-limit ownership, charge twelve movement plus two half-attack units after validation, and clear the exact slot only after a successful transaction under `FD-SPELL-002`. `FD-COMBAT-008` removes presentation delay from Castle's 128-sample LOS, `FD-COMBAT-009` bounds its unseen-target scan to validated slots, and `FD-COMBAT-010` makes projectile-to-melee replacement actor-owned. Castle's pre-direction movement-submode Guard check, possessed-character auto-guard, friendly swaps, spell-field collision, target-everybody Guard omission, permanent-Tangle monster movement, and nonordinary spell/projectile branches remain explicit unresolved boundaries. A routed monster without a retained target and a mandatory ally at the edge report narrow unavailable reasons because Castle's corresponding branches are unsafe or internally ineffective.
- `CombatState` owns bleeding recipients and once-per-battle Turn Undead use; `GameState` owns sorted persistent-Auto character IDs. Both are optional backward-compatible fields inside the existing save aggregate. Castle clears Auto when `killbody` removes a defeated character from battle, including the above-minus-ten bleeding range; party removal does the same, and restore rejects stale or nonliving IDs.
- Auto Turn and persistent character Auto share one rules-owned deterministic activation routine. It uses only existing legal probes, preserves Castle's automatic Bandage-before-Turn-Undead priority and tagged draws, stops at manual, mandatory, error, or terminal boundaries, and rolls state plus RNG back together on its bounded operation limit. Delay is fresh-activation-only; `FD-COMBAT-012` advances a last-slot delay into the next round instead of reproducing Castle's duplicate activation. Manual Bandage exposes one actual living bleeding recipient under `FD-COMBAT-013`; Turn Undead retains source target order, threshold, experience, effect, death-macro, and once-per-battle state.
- Combat Undo is a narrow activation-start position/cursor contract, not generic rollback. Movement without a result retains it; attacks, spells, item effects, reactions, or turn advancement invalidate it. Save state records only actor, start cell, round, turn index, and availability. `FD-COMBAT-014` rejects an occupied start cell instead of reproducing Castle's unchecked field overwrite. Repeatability and initiative-edge re-entry remain fixture-required.
- `BattlefieldView` may expose the stable active-landlook asset identity needed to render Castle's composited battle art. This is detached presentation metadata only; terrain values, passability, LOS, occupants, targets, and movement legality remain simulation-owned battlefield facts.
- A defeated monster with a death macro retains its battlefield footprint until the nested macro completes. `FD-COMBAT-007` removes the footprint only if the monster remains dead and retains it after CODE 119 revival, so a live combatant can never become unpositioned or make the save aggregate invalid.
- Classic random monster-weapon tables have one rules-owned definition shared by construction and package-readiness validation. Every possible generated item ID must exist in immutable package content; combat never treats an unresolved generated weapon as unarmed.
- Monster blindness and petrification use save seven. Blindness writes permanent `-1` before physical damage; petrification writes Castle's target-specific sentinel, sets health to zero, and skips the already-rolled physical damage through the force-kill result.
- Character vault imports arrive as detached validated state plus provenance. The active session clones the state; it never writes back to the vault implicitly. Finalized new characters may request explicit publication only through a typed, saveable confirmation; acceptance emits a committed host event and never performs repository I/O inside the core.
- Active portrait and tactical-icon changes are separate stable-ID session mutations. Every nonempty role is validated against immutable package content during submission and restore; an explicit empty identity remains empty rather than receiving substituted art. Changes consume no RNG or time and never publish a vault revision implicitly.
- Camp is session-owned exploration mode. Entry/explicit-exit time, service clearing, and persistence follow Castle; the player-facing command is not a fixed-duration heal. One Rest intent is one source-held pulse: fatigue changes before five scaled time clicks, and the clock owns hourly conditions/fatigue/spell recovery plus half-day health and exact item-877 charge/load consumption. Poison damage and positive-condition decay precede half-day recovery, so Castle's signed Poisoned term offsets the earlier damage rather than granting a net bonus. Land and dungeon movement leave camp through their distinct pre-movement time costs. Timed and random interruption plus battle return persist the owning Rest or requested movement exactly once.
- Crossing midnight creates one save-owned post-clock continuation after ordered age acknowledgement. It scans timed records by stable source order, advances a same-day record before chance and requirement gates, persists the scan cursor and RNG, and resumes its AP interaction before later random rectangles. `FD-EXPLORATION-001` guards y with the authored y field and uses semantic attempted/current/committed party coordinates; `FD-EXPLORATION-002` performs half-day recovery once per midnight rather than once per dispatched record. A timed AP may rebase the remaining scan after moving the party. Location-changing AP destination semantics still require their dedicated end-to-end fixture.
- At each genuine field-time hour, party fatigue increases by one within Castle's 4–135 bounds. Every positive party condition decays once, then Torch Lit decays once more when still positive; this preserves the source's distinct `30 * power - 1` light-duration scale. Expiration is a state event, and presentation must rebuild from that state rather than reproduce Castle's stale incremental-redraw edge.
- Providence's cell movement cost is a Classic timeclick count, not elapsed minutes. Successful and ordinary positive-tile blocked land movement apply the five-minute outdoor scale and full hourly rules; dungeon movement applies one-minute clicks. A blocked topology probe retains its destination cell, leaves coordinates unchanged, and may continue through current-cell random checks. An ordinary solid dungeon wall consumes no movement time. Zero/negative land cells, boat/shore cancellation, and special dungeon wall bits remain explicit rather than inheriting this bounded rule.
- Every character owns five fixed typed scroll slots. Field scribing and use validate exact case, parchment, spell, power, target, cost, and slot before mutation. A rejected or cancelled target cannot spend spell points, parchment, or a scroll. Combat use, invalid-field discard, and case-plus-scroll transfer remain unavailable until independently adjudicated.
- Unsuspended held-over allies are consumed into the combat roster as non-traitors. After combat, surviving friendly monsters with nonzero `canSummon` eligibility return only through the typed Classic body-count selection; negative eligibility is mandatory. Monster targeting compares allegiance, so hostile monsters can attack party characters or friendly monsters and friendly monsters target hostiles.
- A scenario-owned total defeat is a session handoff, not a completed VM operation. The save aggregate owns the advanced issuing frame, caller metadata, combat defeat, exploration continuation, and Party Death hook together. Opcode 119 revival resumes the ordinary caller without rewards and publishes one battle return; unrecovered defeat closes. Special Castle callers whose behavior is not equivalent remain explicitly unavailable.

## Work Guidance

- `ItemView` resolves Castle-visible Describe facts before crossing the session boundary. Unworn cursed records use their native `iscurse` decoy definition for text and statistics while retaining the original icon; wearing reveals the original record. Presentation must not infer this link or receive the hidden original identity through visible fields.
- Prefer small domain modules behind a fixed `RealmzRules` facade; do not add registries or profile selectors.
- Keep character, condition/time, inventory/economy, combat, magic, and monster behavior in their owned rule modules. Opcode handlers adapt Classic records to these rules instead of duplicating formulas.
- Preserve 16-bit and 32-bit arithmetic semantics explicitly where Castle behavior depends on them.
- Keep serialized IDs stable strings and use `StringName` only as an internal lookup optimization.

## Verification

- `tools/verify_architecture.ps1` rejects forbidden host dependencies and direct randomness.
- Core behavior requires headless unit tests and, when source-backed, an evidence-labelled oracle fixture.

## Child DOX Index

- No child AGENTS.md files are currently required; subdirectories remain governed here.

class_name BattleDefinition
extends RefCounted

var id: String
var classic_id: int
var distance: int
var message_before_id: int
var message_after_id: int
var macro_id: int
var _monster_slots: Array[BattleMonsterSlotDefinition]


func _init(definition_id: String, native_id: int, battle_monster_slots: Array[BattleMonsterSlotDefinition], battle_distance: int = 0, before_message: int = 0, after_message: int = 0, battle_macro: int = 0) -> void:
	id = definition_id
	classic_id = native_id
	_monster_slots = battle_monster_slots.duplicate()
	distance = battle_distance
	message_before_id = before_message
	message_after_id = after_message
	macro_id = battle_macro


func monster_slots() -> Array[BattleMonsterSlotDefinition]:
	return _monster_slots.duplicate()

# Gameplay domain evidence

This document records the Phase 4 evidence boundary. Castle source observations guide the fixed rules and Classic opcode adapters; runtime tests prove the new implementation. Content inventory does not by itself prove Castle executable parity or campaign reachability.

## Castle source/control-flow

Pinned oracle: Realmz Castle commit `491816ad60037394f92c428e99c004494d3c28b3`.

- `src/realmz_orig/newland.c:1966-2003` loads the packed spell ID and applies power, save adjustment, and force-affect fields for opcodes 17 and 18. `src/realmz_orig/resolvespell.c:13-61` rolls base duration, one duration contribution per power level, base damage, and one damage contribution per power level in that order. Lines 286-365 apply saves, elemental protection, condition additions, and condition clears. The 2.0 rule keeps that draw order and packed identity rather than treating scenario-spell slots as zero-based runtime IDs.
- `src/realmz_orig/modify-cancast.c:47-69`, `getup.c:58-101,257-267`, `castspell.c:210-237,714-734`, `combatinfo-combatchoice.c:529-540`, `loadspell.c:5-18`, `combat.c:124-379`, `getrange.c:5-89`, `resist.c:5-101`, `resolvespell.c:13-61,270-365`, and `misc.c:1188-1229` establish ordinary character and monster spell admission and resolution. A nonzero scenario flag blocks casting; the source conditions, same-round attack, and per-activation limits also gate it. The Classic ID encodes zero-based tier independently of caster level. Character commits spend spell points, two half-attacks, and twelve movement. Monster commits sample ten fixed slots, preserve initial range power while lowering only affordability power, sample native party-gap-monster target space, clear Guard/movement, and can retry once after moving. A failed charm opposed save continues into screens, Animated immunity, and magic resistance; `cannot` bypasses those later checks only after consuming the first draw. Realmz 2.0 exposes typed player combinations and implements ordinary single-actor damage for players plus ordinary opposed-party-or-monster damage for monsters; the following records own bounded group, spatial, and healing branches. Friendly `cannot == 4` outside strict special-57 healing, class-nine, other special, zero-damage, and anomalous nonpositive-cost paths remain explicit. Castle's pre-paid player cancellation, negative-cost SP increase, post-range size bonus, and target-everybody Guard omission remain recorded rather than normalized.
- `src/realmz_orig/resolvespell.c:220,396,424`, `killbody.c:4-127`, `emptyque.c:5-13`, `combat.c:1091`, `getup.c:69`, and `newland.c:292-307` establish the spell-death-macro lifecycle. Every monster killed while `inspell` appends its death macro to `todoque`; Castle drains those records in order before normal combat progression. The queued `killbody` branch does not reset `traiter`, whereas authored opcode 119 independently revives the macro subject and explicitly clears it. Realmz 2.0 therefore owns an ordered spell macro queue, original caster cursor, deferred turn decision, and exact completed-subject identity in `CombatState` and the session/VM continuation. The queue survives typed interaction and save/restore; each still-dead completed subject loses occupancy before the next macro, and battle outcome or caster advancement waits for the queue to empty. This fixes the prior immediate-single-macro host path without attributing opcode 119's authored allegiance change to every death macro. Automatic groups and bounded spatial areas feed that queue through one shared cost/base-duration/base-damage transaction.
- `src/realmz_orig/combatinfo-combatchoice.c:663-705`, `resolvespell.c:13-61,254-433`, and `spelltargets.c:61-92` establish player automatic-group targeting. Types 9, 10, and 12 build friendly, enemy, and everybody tracks in party-slot then monster-slot order. One `resolvespell` call rolls duration and base damage once before per-target resistance, save, protection, damage, and `killbody`; player cost is already committed by `castspell`. Realmz 2.0 implements that bounded ordinary-damage path with one targetless typed picker option and the existing ordered spell death-macro queue. Castle's separate monster branches in `combat.c:162-207` jump to resolution before assigning `powerlevel`, checking affordability, deducting spell points, or clearing movement; type 12 also omits the Guard clear used by 9 and 10. Those likely stale-global/resource bugs remain explicitly disabled as `monster-group-spell-power-resource-anomaly`. Providence's editor correction adds source-backed target value 12 without changing schema v2's existing numeric projection. Target type 11's fallthrough into the player all-enemy `else` remains outside this case.
- `src/realmz_orig/main.c`, `combatinfo-combatchoice.c:663-705`, `cast.c`, `spelltargets.c`, and `resolvespell.c:13-61,254-433` establish player spatial targeting. Castle loads eighteen 7x7 masks from Data AD. Type 3 selects one center and uses the authored `size`; type 4 substitutes cast power; `spelltargets` scans the selected mask in row-major order, deduplicates occupied field IDs, removes monsters above 100 magic resistance, and `resolvespell` rolls duration/base damage once before party-slot then monster-slot defenses. Type 0 is materially different: it permits `powerlevel` independent selections and calls targeting/resolution for each, so it is not implemented as an area. Realmz 2.0 owns the masks as fixed rules data, exposes exact offsets and legal centers, validates range/LOS and full-field safety before mutation, and uses the existing shared multi-target and death-macro transaction. Presentation now selects and previews those facts directly on the battlefield, preserving repeated-target click order without reconstructing legality. Providence schema v2 already preserves target type, size, rotation, queue icon, range, and ordinary spell fields; no compiler change is required. Castle's unsafe edge indexing, reflection draw/redirect, adjacent-mask rotation, and persistent queued-field lifecycle remain explicit unavailable boundaries.
- `src/realmz_orig/castspeffect.c`, `moving.c`, `resolvespeffect.c`, `resolvespell.c`, `damage.c`, and `attack.c` establish the bounded combat-feedback families. Cast start uses `cicn 11992 + lookStart * 8`; moving spells use PICT 302 battle tile `200 + lookStart`; ordinary resolution presents exactly eight CIcons beginning at 12032 when `lookEnd` is zero or `11992 + lookEnd * 8` otherwise. Result handlers use CIcons 159–167 for condition, armed impact, unarmed impact, elemental, and magic feedback, with a fixed centered number rather than an upward float. Positive sounds may overlap and negative sounds block later presentation. Realmz Rebuilt publishes those exact non-save-owned identities in ordered committed events, lets scenario media override application media by exact key, and delays the final detached view until cosmetic playback settles. The pinned application fork contains spell frames 12000–12127 but not 11992–11999, even though 65 standard package spells author `lookStart` zero; that source/content inconsistency remains an exact unavailable diagnostic rather than receiving substituted art. CIcon 161 contains red splash pixels but Castle source does not call it blood or gore; CIcon 167 has a magic handler name without a traced caller; death CIcon use remains observation-required.
- `src/realmz_orig/combatinfo-combatchoice.c:645-648,1227-1423`, `cast.c:18-44`, `spelltargets.c:5-105`, `resolvespell.c:13-61,254-433`, and `combat.c:9-12,209-370` establish repeated target type 0. With size zero, a player chooses up to `powerlevel` distinct party or monster actors in an explicit order and may cast after the first selection; the already chosen power determines the one spell-point cost. `cast` invokes targeting and resolution separately for each selection, so duration and base damage reroll per actor. A monster rolls range power, then target power from the current in-range count, lowers it only for affordability, and samples unique party/gap/monster native slots. Castle's local `pass` leaks across the whole battle and can make a later cast abort before sampling. `FD-COMBAT-011`, recorded by `monster-spell-target-retry-scope-correction.json`, scopes the hundred-attempt guard to one cast while preserving a genuine within-cast partial result and full chosen-power cost; the guard is not persisted. Providence commit `fa0297426677552080608e1b89bad4334d323465` corrects the editor's open-space-only label while retaining schema-v2 numeric fields. Nonzero-size open-space/summoning placement remains explicit. Castle's partial abort refund is not reproduced: the typed host mutates only after an explicit committed Cast response.
- `src/realmz_orig/spelltargets.c:94-111`, `cast.c:18-44`, `combat.c:147-378`, `getrange.c:5-58`, `resolvespell.c:254-433`, `resist.c:5-101`, `killbody.c:87-97`, `emptyque.c:5-13`, and `getup.c:42-69` establish ordinary spell reflection and mixed monster target slots. A selected party or monster actor with Reflecting Spells consumes `Rand(100)` and results below 34 replace that actor with active caster `q[up]` before duration, damage, the original monster's over-100 exclusion, resistance, saves, or protection. The redirected actor is resolved once and cannot reflect recursively. Target type zero repeats the complete check per selection; monster casters may select opposed monsters at native slots ten onward. If reflection kills a monster caster, Castle queues its death macro while `inspell` is true, finishes the remaining `noofmagattacks` iterations without another caster-stamina check, and drains the queue in `getup`. Because monster damage calls `killbody` for every nonpositive result, later reflected hits append duplicate records for that caster to the fixed 100-entry `todoque`; `emptyque` executes records, not unique subjects. Realmz 2.0 preserves selected and effective target IDs, that bounded record order, subject occupancy through its final duplicate, and the complete saveable caster continuation. Castle's automatic groups bypass this check, area footprints and intelligent scoring can consume anomalous repeated reflection draws, and queued fields pass `noreflect`; those branches remain separate rather than inheriting ordinary behavior.
- `src/realmz_orig/combatinfo-combatchoice.c:1227-1423`, `combat.c:209-370`, `getrange.c:5-89`, `spelltargets.c:5-111`, `resist.c:5-101`, `resolvespell.c:13-61,186-190,254-433`, `heal.c:5-47`, `killbody.c:26-52,149-152`, and `structs.h:159-170` establish special-57 combat healing. Manual player targeting permits any living party or monster actor; monster `cannot == 4` reverses allegiance and may select the caster itself. Reflection and resistance occur before special 57 negates rolled damage. Party healing rejects stone and dead characters and caps at maximum stamina. Although `heal` itself can revive an unconscious character, combat `killbody` has already removed that actor from the targetable field; the combat picker therefore exposes living actors only. Monster healing subtracts negative damage directly, may exceed maximum stamina, uses signed-short storage, and still sets `beenattacked`. Realmz 2.0 implements only the source-shaped target-one, class-eight, damage-type-eight, positive-cost special-57 form, exposes detached party-then-monster options, publishes signed damage plus positive healing, and persists over-maximum monster stamina without weakening signed-range validation. Camp healing, specials 58 through 60, other zero-damage effects, and generic stock spell display names remain separately flagged.
- `src/realmz_orig/structs.h:159-170`, `combatsetup.c:277-315`, and `spelltargets.c:101-104` establish monster starting-condition ownership. Data MD stores forty signed bytes directly inside each monster record; battle setup reads the complete struct before runtime adjustments, and ordinary targeting consults the resulting Reflecting Spells slot. Providence commit `b045a6317712f95932b7334490ecd8f756d43e5b` corrects schema-v2 data loss by requiring and emitting all forty values. The runtime validates their signed-byte range and copies them into both ordinary and authored-battle monster instances before play. The regenerated synthetic fixture uses permanent reflection to prove the compiler, loader, and construction path without embedding commercial records.
- `src/realmz_orig/misc.c:1651-1667`, `race.c:5-47,178-206`, and `class.c:5-41,183-207` establish character profile identity. Character race and caste values start at one; each creator enumerates thirty slots, and `loadprofile` subtracts one before seeking the fixed Data Race or Data Caste record. Race eligibility stores thirty caste columns at zero-based record positions. Providence commit `1d660bb6dbab175e641f33d07e8755e8ee3be24e` caps both native tables at thirty records, emits stable one-based identities and imported names, and aligns both eligibility directions. Schema and runtime validation independently require one unique profile for every Classic ID 1 through 30.
- `newcharacter.c::CharacterGen`, `getnumspells.c::getnumspells`, and `spellselect.c::Spellselect` establish the staged level-one creator boundary. One generated character reaches Review before acceptance; reroll repeats the source RNG path, while acceptance retains the reviewed result. Spell points use the caste start-level sum, current level, and Knowledge or Judgment; costs are 1, 3, 6, 10, 15, 21, and 28. The character table is exactly seven by twelve even though the resource-name catalog has fifteen entries per level. Realmz 2.0 therefore excludes slots thirteen through fifteen, persists the provisional character and spell choices, and yields a typed confirmation when points remain.
- `misc.c::Startlevel`, `newcharacter.c::NewCharacter`, `levelup.c::levelup`, and `misc.c::getexp` establish the advanced-character workflow over fixed levels 1, 3, 5, 7, 9, 11, 13, 15, 17, 20, 25, and 30. Castle constructs the level-one base, sets prestige to ten times the square of target-minus-one and direct experience to the negative caste victory threshold, then invokes ordinary `levelup` once per additional level before starting spells and initial items. Realmz 2.0 uses the same fixed choices through the campaign maximum, preserves each registration-era draw and level-up field order, and retains the generated character as the session-owned Review draft.
- `structs.h:60,94,314` and `updatespec.c:49-97` establish separate twelve-slot racial combat modifiers and fifteen-slot trained abilities, but only fourteen race/caste ability inputs. Castle's fifteenth loop iteration reads adjacent struct fields. `FD-CHARACTER-001` keeps the unauthored character ability slot zero and draw-free while preserving all fourteen authored initialization, Strength/Dexterity adjustment, level-up dice, and clamp rules. `levelup.c:35-44` also establishes that a reached caste condition threshold replaces any nonnegative condition with permanent `-1`; only an already-negative sentinel decrements.
- `src/realmz_orig/newland.c:2597-2662` pools and removes party wealth/equipment for opcode 36, then restores the exact stored records and returns items acquired in the interim separately. The 2.0 equivalent stores detached item instances and wealth in `PartyState`, persists the escrow, restores equipment, recalculates load from immutable item definitions, and moves interim finds to party storage.
- `src/realmz_orig/newcharacter.c:13-39`, `misc.c:824-839`, `wear.c:5-226`, `removeitem.c:5-102`, `moveicon.c:221-259,353-440,615-655`, `dropitem.c:5-29`, `items.c:470-549,885-1000`, and `showitems-showspecial.c:256-351` establish starting and ordinary carried-item workflows. `addinitialitems` visits the caste's authored slots in order, admits only records that fit, marks them identified, preserves authored charges, attempts to wear each admitted item, then adds starting gold; `calcw` derives load from gold, gems, jewelry at fifteen units each, and every item's base-plus-charge weight. Castle increments its separate `numitems` before the capacity test; Realmz 2.0 does not manufacture blank item records when an overweight record is skipped. Finalization uses package definitions for these identities and weights, vault import recomputes load against the target package, and restore rejects a mismatched saved total transactionally. Race and caste both admit the item's first category bit before specific race/caste and descriptor/class exclusions; equipment then enforces one slot per type above one, two nonduplicate rings, two hands, an equipped quiver for ordinary bows, party-unique negative-cost items, and curse identification/removal lock. Trade checks the recipient's thirty-item and load limits, accepts an equipped record, and writes it unequipped on the recipient. `FD-INVENTORY-001` follows that ordinary record outcome but prevents Castle's direct-delete path from bypassing a curse or retaining stale derived source bonuses. Drop removes one exact unequipped record after confirmation. Realmz 2.0 owns those operations through typed probes, intents, detached disabled reasons, and a saveable drop continuation. Charged spell effects are owned by the next bounded case; passive effects that need other character-state mutation, field identification, and split/join remain unavailable instead of partially mutating state. Castle split/join changes stack records without consistently changing carried load even though trade weighs each record; that contradiction requires a named fidelity decision before exposure. Remake's Honest Storage is not Castle's opcode-36 escrow and is not presented as a Classic player service.
- `src/realmz_orig/items.c:566-735`, `showitems-showspecial.c:256-351`, `getchoice.c:5-198`, and `combatinfo-combatchoice.c:289-307` establish the common charged spell-item path. An item with `sp2 > 1100` and a positive instance charge or negative authored charge loads that spell, validates `canuse`, derives power from `abs(sp1)` with value eight calling `Rand(7)`, and enforces combat/camp availability. A positive charge and `xcharge` load are removed before targeting; negative charges are retained. The source requests item sound plus 600, uses self for target type 5, all party records for field target types above 2, and `getchoice` for the remaining field targets, while combat returns through its ordinary spell target state. Realmz 2.0 implements fixed-power field self/party and combat actor/automatic-group forms plus field `Rand(7)` staging through one typed item-use contract; it spends no spell points, persists the pending field selection, and publishes exact item/target/charge/sound provenance. Castle ignores the field picker's return after decrementing the charge, so cancellation appears to lose a charge; that suspicious branch remains oracle-required. Door/XAP items, type-13 scrolls, missile-class items, random-power combat, spatial/repeated combat targets, and broader spell specials remain separate explicit families.
- `src/realmz_orig/moveicon.c:5-24,27-173,528-657`, `items.c:885-925`, `choice.c:362-430`, and `getselection.c:5-8` establish the ordinary shop lifecycle. Shop stock is identified; buy cost uses absolute value, inflation, and a 32000 cap; sale uses integer half cost, current/authored charge condition, inflation capped at 100 percent, then an unidentified divide-by-fifty penalty. Ordinary selection refuses equipped sale. Purchases spend pooled then selected-character gold, while sales add to the pool and return the item to matching or first-empty category stock. Paid identification spends twenty gold on one selected instance and plays sound 683. Realmz 2.0 preserves those player-visible outcomes through one typed, saveable continuation and hides true carried-item identity until identification. `FD-ECONOMY-001` gives zero-charge definitions full condition instead of Castle's non-finite conversion. Providence retains occupied stock order but not empty native slot indices, so normalized buyback identity and quantity are save-owned while exact first-empty ordering remains an explicit compiler gap.
- `src/realmz_orig/newland.c:2562-2571,3133-3140`, `buttonchoice.c:413-443`, `temple.c:5-222`, `heal.c:5-40`, `spelllist.c:5-112`, `pool.c:5-37`, and `share-movecost-dialog.c:5-62` establish the ordinary temple lifecycle. Opcode 32 stores availability and a signed cost percentage; the player later enters through the application command after global macro 5. Temple exposes nine fixed services, scales their costs through float arithmetic into a short, spends pooled then selected-character gold, and requests sound 10129 on every service attempt. Healing excludes stone and health below -9. The four direct cures clear disease, stone, poison, and blindness; remove curse clears condition 3 and force-removes curse-linked equipment; Revive clears Animated and Stone after its conditional health/ability mutation. Concurrent bank availability moves all pooled denominations from bank on entry and back on exit. Realmz 2.0 implements that typed, saveable subset. Global macro 5 remains a compiler/application gap; no-bank Swap and movement cleanup are now owned by the separate pooled-wealth departure case. Castle's negative signed percentage can increase pooled gold; this suspicious outcome is preserved pending authored evidence for a correction.
- `src/realmz_orig/pool.c:5-21`, `share-movecost-dialog.c:5-40`, `swap.c:5-198`, `buttonchoice.c:38-104,563-570`, `checkmoneypool.c:5-24`, `moveparty.c:6-38`, `threed.c:315-421`, `question.c:5-72`, and `misc.c:51-98` establish the ordinary money workspace and departure guard. Pool moves all three personal denominations to the shared pool and removes gold/gem load at one each and jewelry load at fifteen. Share redistributes jewelry, gems, then gold one unit per character per pass. Swap selects one character and moves five gold or one gem or jewelry per held step, checks complete load only in the pool-to-character direction, recalculates movement, and uses sounds 10051 or 663. `FD-ECONOMY-003` corrects Share's contradictory current-load-only jewelry check; every other order, increment, load, sound, and persistence fact remains source-backed. The direct Services workspace uses one synchronous typed intent per Classic increment and a detached availability model. Its presentation-owned ordinary-route lifecycle requests button sound 141, stops existing channels before modal sound 3003, and requests Done sound 141 without adding simulation state or replaying those sounds for typed Shop, Temple, or Bank interactions. With no bank, Castle resolves a nonempty pool before destination passability: sound 20005 precedes a yes/no boundary; No clears the pool, while Yes opens Swap and clears the remainder on Done. Both ordinary land and dungeon callers then continue the original movement attempt. The early return after accepted distribution is confined to an internal `moveparty` fallback that ordinary callers have already guarded. Realmz 2.0 preserves the ordinary branch through a typed, saveable continuation. Contextual money-changing rates remain separate, the unavailable STR# prompt wording is explicitly synthetic, and Castle's blocked-attempt time remains an evidenced movement gap rather than an economy assumption.
- `src/realmz_orig/newland.c:1736-1823` copies XAP programs over encounter/AP programs or redirects the active AP. The 2.0 runtime records equivalent program mappings and active-frame redirects without modifying immutable package definitions.
- `src/realmz_orig/attack.c:199-238,608-625`, `newland.c:351-404`, `getbattleorder.c:5-80`, `removeitem.c:5-92`, `dropitem.c:5-29`, `booty.c:130-177,320-340,470-510,690-710,1440-1600`, and `pref.c:518-740` establish natural fumbles, forced fumbles, and post-battle recovery. Character attacks always consume `Rand(1000 + 100 * level)` when fumbles are enabled; only 51–59 with a removable melee weapon and queue capacity drops it and forces a miss, calling synchronous 10121/10123 before `dropitem` adds asynchronous 655. Armed monsters use `Rand(600 + 50 * hit dice)` and fumble on 21–34 by clearing only the active weapon with synchronous 10121/655. Opcode 122's outer `q[up] < 10` guard excludes monster initiative IDs despite its nested monster branch, so it affects only an active party combatant after a physical action. Castle runs body count before booty, inserts fumble IDs first, retains them after retreat, identifies them, and lets the player choose a recipient subject to inventory/load limits. `FD-COMBAT-005` preserves the exact item instance and remaining charges instead of Castle's ID-only reconstruction. The global `allowfumble` preference and its linked five-percent XP adjustment, plus the live `inspell` opcode guard, remain explicit unresolved settings/lifecycle boundaries.

An equipped Classic type-2 item is the weapon even when its magic plus is zero; damage bonuses on rings or armor continue to contribute without changing an unarmed character into an armed one. This is not complete tactical combat. ## Party Order workflow

- Castle `handlemenuchoice.c::HandleMenuChoice` dispatches the Character-menu command to `save-direction-order.c::order`. `order` collects one complete ordinal assignment through `getchoice`, permutes full character structs, rebuilds the per-slot defined-spell cache, and redraws. This establishes a whole-party transaction rather than repeated gameplay swaps.
- Castle's abort path is internally unsafe: `getchoice.c::getchoice` clears every `track` entry before returning, while `order` does not test a result and still evaluates `c[track[t] - 1]`. `party-order-abort-correction.json` records `FD-CHARACTER-003`; 2.0 Cancel discards its presentation draft and commits nothing.
- Remake's `CharPickButton._drop_data` swaps selected party buttons and `CharSwapRect._on_OKButton_pressed` replaces active roster membership. Those are partial donor behaviors only; neither is authority for the Classic ordering lifecycle.
- Realmz 2.0 accepts one exact stable-ID permutation through `PlayerIntent.REORDER_PARTY`, preserves the existing `CharacterState` objects, emits previous/current order, and persists the party array. Focused tests cover complete mutation, duplicate/unknown/solo rejection, RNG stability, state preservation, save/restore, presentation staging, Apply, Cancel, and unavailable combat state.

## Character inspection workflow

- Castle `viewcharacter.c::viewcharacter` composes the main statistics sheet and dispatches separate equipment, condition, special-modifier, trained-ability, spell, race, caste, aging, and prestige views. `ShowStats`, `showcondition`, `showspecial`, `Race`, and `Caste` establish the visible fields and their source ordering.
- Providence schema v2 already preserves the immutable race/caste descriptions, traits, five age ranges/change rows, appearance identities, item data, and spell data needed by those views. No compiler or package migration is required.
- `character-age-inspection-correction.json` records `FD-CHARACTER-004`. Castle's Aging branch derives the highlighted row from age and writes `currentagegroup` during inspection; 2.0 derives an immutable `CharacterAgeBandView.active` value and leaves `CharacterState` unchanged.
- Castle's prestige display is not a penalty-only field. It combines lifetime hit, miss, damage, kill, death, knockout, turn, spell, and destroyed-foe counters with the penalty. Until those counters and every mutation owner exist, the detached view exposes an exact unavailable reason instead of fabricating a zero record.
- Some trained-ability display names are loaded from native STR# resources absent from the pinned source tree. Exact slots and signed values remain visible under explicit generic labels; names are not inferred from Remake or adjacent indices.

## Active character appearance workflow

- Castle `handlemenuchoice.c::HandleMenuChoice` dispatches separate portrait and tactical-icon commands through `modify-cancast.c::modify`. `portrait-picklock.c::portrait` recommends six portraits from the race record's `defaulticonset`; `iconpict.c::iconpicture` independently recommends six tactical icons from the character's one-based race. The runtime retains this distinction rather than assuming one shared recommendation formula.
- Castle copies the picker result into the active party slot and then rewrites the standalone Character Files record. `active-character-appearance-ownership-correction.json` records `FD-CHARACTER-005`: Realmz 2.0 previews locally, applies one exact role through `GameSession`, discards without mutation, and never publishes a vault revision implicitly.
- Providence schema v2 already provides all 120 portraits, all 120 tactical icons, exact role/resource identities, race Classic IDs, and `defaultIconSet`; no compiler change is required.
- Focused tests prove independent portrait/icon mutation, exact events, no RNG or clock change, wrong-role and unknown-character rejection, save/restore, package-role validation during transactional restore, explicit empty-media preservation without substitution, full-catalog detached views, and presentation-only preview/discard.
